title: watchOS 27.2 Code Hints at iPhone-Style Screenshot Previews
content:
watchOS 27.2 could introduce a feature that lets Apple Watch screenshots be previewed with options to share or delete, similar to how screenshots work on the iPhone.


Signs of the feature were found in watchOS 27.2 by code explorer pdfu. The option is hidden behind a feature flag that's not enabled, but it could be introduced in a later watchOS 27.2 beta.


A new screenshot experience is coming to Apple Watch, inspired by iPhone.
Hidden behind a feature flag in watchOS 27.2, it lets you preview, share, or delete a screenshot right after taking it. pic.twitter.com/MT5wmDjRnq
— pdfu (@itspdfu) September 24, 2026
 

Right now, taking a screenshot on the Apple Watch sends it directly to the iPhone Photos app with no confirmation screen. It's easy to accidentally take a screenshot since it only requires pressing the Digital Crown and side button at the same time.

On the iPhone, taking a screenshot shows either a full-screen preview or a thumbnail preview depending on your settings, but both options let you save, share, or delete the screenshot with a couple taps.

title: Beats 360 Headphones Now Available in Apple Stores
content:
The new Beats 360 headphones are available for purchase at many Apple Stores around the world as of today. Retailers like Best Buy and Target also have some stock available in stores.


Apple's Beats brand announced the headphones earlier this week after teasing them for several months. The Beats 360 are over-ear headphones with a design similar to the AirPods Max and interchangeable ear cushions so you can swap colors.

Compared with the Beats Studio Pro, the Beats 360 have up to 1.75x more noise cancellation and improved sound quality. Features like Personalized Spatial Audio, Transparency mode, and Adaptive EQ are supported, as are fast pairing and automatic device switching. They have IPX4 sweat and water resistance, making them suitable for the gym.

The Beats 360 work with two kinds of cushions. The Performance Knit memory foam cushions are breathable and meant for working out, while the UltraPlush cushions have a softer, more pillowy feel. The Beats 360 ship with the Performance Knit cushions, and the UltraPlush can be purchased separately.

priced at $349.99, and for a limited time, Apple is selling add-on ear cushions for a discounted $9.99 price through October 31. Headphone colors include Black, Cloud, Pink, and Sky. The Performance Knit cushions come in Black, Cloud, Pink, Sky, Navy, and Volt, while the UltraPlush come in Black and Cloud.

title: Apple Shares New Video Promoting iOS 27 Parental Controls
content:
Apple today shared a video promoting the new parental control features it added in iOS 27.



Apple says Child Accounts are easier to set up in ‌iOS 27‌ and more intuitive to use. Improved controls allow parents to choose the types of apps children have access to, while Ask to Buy lets kids request new apps and games.

FaceTime detects and blocks both violence and nudity in images and videos.

Time Allowances and Schedules let parents customize what children can access by the day, hour, and activity, with options to limit apps during school hours. There are one-tap controls to pause access entirely during family events like dinnertime or allow unlimited screen time.

Apple's updated parental controls come as the company deals with regulatory pressure over child safety in countries like the UK, U.S., and Australia. The UK has called for device-level controls that keep kids from viewing and sharing inappropriate images, while the U.S. Kids Internet and Digital Safety Act is now in the Senate. Australia has already prohibited children under 16 from creating accounts on certain social media apps.

iPadOS 27, and macOS Golden Gate. Every device in a Family Sharing group needs to be running the latest software for the Screen Time update to work.

title: The iPhone Duo’s odd shape actually has a very cool name
content:
Macworld





The upcoming iPhone Duo’s form has widely been referred to as a having a “similar size to a passport,” comparing it to an object most people are familiar with. But an article by British GQ last week points out that the shape is based on the A-size paper format that’s used internationally.
A Macworld Podcast listener provides some specifics:
I wanted to comment on the aspect ratio of the Duo’s outer and inner screens – both about 1.4 : 1. As an ex-graphic designer, this ratio (known as the silver ratio, 1 to the square root of 2) is very well known to me. That is because in the UK and Europe all our paper sizes are based on this ratio. 
A4 is 297 x 210mm which when folded exactly in half results in A5, which has the same ratio. This continues with smaller sizes of A6, etc. Going the other way, A3 is double A4, etc, until you get to A0, which has a surface area of 1 metre squared. Neat eh? 
The iPhone Duo therefore is like an A5 sheet of paper, folded in half when closed, and is something that will have been very familiar with Molly Anderson who (like Jony Ive) is from the UK.  
Stuart G. via email
I don’t know about you, but I prefer referring to the iPhone Duo’s shape as the “silver ratio” instead of “passport style.” It’s catchy and classy. And it’s cool to know that Apple put some serious thought into the form factor and not just arbitrarily picking a shape.
The iPhone Duo was introduced during the “Surprise and Shine” event on September 9. Apple will start taking orders for the iPhone Duo on October 16, and shipments start on October 23. Learn more about the iPhone Duo.

title: Should you buy an Apple Watch now or wait? Best time to buy in 2026
content:
Macworld





Apple’s 2026 Watch lineup is now on sale, with the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 joining the Apple Watch SE 3. That makes this a reasonable time to buy if you want the latest features. If price matters more, compare the new models with discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock – or wait for the October and Black Friday sales. The SE 3 remains the least expensive option in Apple’s current lineup, but it’s also the oldest as it was introduced in September 2025. 
If you don’t need a watch immediately, it’s worth considering the major sales events that follow Apple’s launch. Retailers consistently offer their biggest Apple Watch discounts during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday in November. During Prime Day in June 2026, for example, we saw discounts ranging from $50 to $120 on current models.
In this guide, we’ll explain whether you should buy an Apple Watch now or wait, the best times of year to find the biggest discounts, and how to avoid paying full price just before a new model arrives. Read our Macworld’s Best Apple Watch guide for more buying advice.

Buy an Apple Watch now if…

				
					

				
			
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale alongside the SE 3 and there are no new models expected. Buy now if you need a watch soon or the model you want meets your needs at a price you’re happy to pay. The Series 12 is the best everyday choice, the SE 3 is the best value, and the Ultra 4 makes sense if you need its longer battery life or outdoor features. A discounted Series 11 or Ultra 3 could also be worth buying if you don’t need the latest additions.
You should consider buying now if:
Your current Apple Watch cannot run watchOS 27, or its battery no longer lasts long enough for your needs.
You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model. The current watches offer substantial improvements in displays, performance, health tracking and battery life.
You want the Series 12 or Ultra 4’s new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and Readiness score. Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026, so don’t count on using those immediately.
You would benefit from the Ultra 4’s up to 50-hour battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features.
You need a watch before a trip or event, or you find a worthwhile discount on a model that suits you.


						

							


Don’t buy an Apple Watch now if…
The main reason to wait now is price: retailers may discount the new models during October sales and Black Friday.
You may want to wait or choose a different model if:
You want the lowest possible price and are happy to wait for the next major sale. Compare any Series 12 or Ultra 4 offer with remaining Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock.
You already own a Series 10 or 11 and do not need the Series 12’s new health sensing features. Its quoted everyday battery life remains 24 hours.
You own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life and outdoor features already meet your needs. The Ultra 4’s 50-hour rating is its clearest reason to upgrade.
You are considering a used watch that cannot run watchOS 27. The Series 8, SE 2 and original Ultra, along with older models, miss out on the latest major software update.
You use an Android phone. Apple Watch requires an iPhone.
You are considering the SE 3 but need ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring or the new Health Sensing System. Choose the Series 12 instead.

Should you buy: Buy
The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best choice for most people. Starting at $399/£369 – the same starting price as the Series 11 – it combines Apple’s advanced health features with a smaller, lighter design than the Ultra 4. Its new Health Sensing System measures heart rate every five seconds and heart-rate variability more frequently, providing data for a new Readiness score. The S11 chip also supports Audio Intelligence features, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due to arrive in beta later in 2026. 
Apple still rates everyday battery life at up to 24 hours, the same as Series 11. Outdoor workout tracking lasts longer, however, and a 15-minute charge now provides up to 12 hours of use, compared with around eight hours for Series 11. Aluminum models also gain a tougher Ceramic Shield 2 display. 
Buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:
You’re buying your first Apple Watch or upgrading from a much older model and want the best everyday option.
You want the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, and Readiness score.
You want advanced features missing from the SE 3, including ECG, Blood Oxygen monitoring and hypertension notifications.
You prefer a lighter watch with two size choices over the larger Ultra 4.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch Series 12 if:
You own a Series 10 or 11 that still meets your needs. The new health features may not justify the cost of upgrading, and Apple’s 24-hour everyday battery rating has not changed.
You can get a Series 11 at a meaningful discount and don’t need the new health sensing or upcoming Audio Intelligence features.
You mainly want fitness tracking, notifications and basic safety features. The SE 3 costs $150/£150 less.
You need more than a day of battery life, satellite communication or specialist outdoor features. Consider the Ultra 4 instead.
Our verdict: This is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most people buying a new watch today. Its new health sensing features make it a more substantial upgrade than the Series 11 was, while the starting price has stayed the same. Owners of recent watches should weigh those additions against the cost: a discounted Series 11 – or keeping the watch they already have – may be the better value.

The Apple Watch SE 3 is the best-value Apple Watch in the lineup and the model we’d recommend for most iPhone users. Announced in September 2025, it brought many features that were previously reserved for Apple’s premium watches, including an always-on display, temperature sensing, fast charging and the S10 chip used in the Series 11 and Ultra 3.
If you don’t need Apple’s most advanced health sensors, the SE 3 delivers almost everything that makes the Apple Watch great at a much lower price. It starts at $249 / £219, although we’ve already seen it discounted to $199 during major sales.
The SE 3 also supports Siri AI in watchOS 27 when paired with a compatible Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone. Siri AI is currently in beta and rolling out in English. The SE 3 does not support the separate Audio Intelligence features coming to the Series 12 and Ultra 4, including Live Rewind and Siri Recap.
Buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:
You want the best-value Apple Watch.
You’re buying your first smartwatch.
You mainly want fitness tracking, notifications and Apple’s core smartwatch features.
You want safety features such as Fall Detection, Crash Detection and heart-rate alerts.
You’re buying for a child or older family member, particularly the cellular model.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch SE 3 if:
You need ECG or blood oxygen monitoring, which are only available on the Series 12 and Ultra 4.
You want the brightest display and most premium design—the SE 3 still has thicker bezels than the flagship models.
You need longer battery life. The SE 3 is rated for 18 hours, compared with 24 hours for the Series 12.
You’re happy to spend more for Apple’s most advanced health and fitness features.
Our verdict: The Apple Watch SE 3 is an outstanding budget smartwatch. Its always-on display, S10 processor, fast charging and improved health features make it a huge step up from the SE 2. Unless you specifically need ECG, blood oxygen monitoring or the longer battery life of the Series 11, the SE 3 is the Apple Watch we’d recommend to most buyers.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is Apple’s most capable watch, aimed at endurance athletes, hikers, divers and anyone who regularly spends more than a day away from a charger. It starts at $799/£749, the same starting price as the Ultra 3, and retains the 49mm titanium case, bright display, dual-frequency GPS, satellite communication and diving support. 
Battery life is the strongest reason to choose the new model. Apple rates the Ultra 4 for up to 50 hours of normal use, up from 42 hours on Ultra 3, or 84 hours in Low Power Mode, up from 72. Its new Extended Workout modes can track outdoor activity for up to 25 hours with full GPS and heart-rate readings, or up to 45 hours in Max Extended Workout mode. Like the Series 12, it gains the new Health Sensing System, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings, and a Readiness score. Its S11 chip supports Audio Intelligence, although Live Rewind and Siri Recap are due in beta later in 2026. 
Buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You want the longest battery life available on an Apple Watch, particularly for travel, long shifts or time away from a charger.
You need extended outdoor workout tracking, precision dual-frequency GPS or satellite communication.
You hike, dive or take part in endurance sports and will use its rugged case, Action button and specialist features.
You want the new Health Sensing System in an Ultra watch and are upgrading from a substantially older model.
Don’t buy the Apple Watch Ultra 4 if:
You already own an Ultra 3 and its 42-hour battery life meets your needs. It retains many of the same outdoor features, including satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS.
You find an Ultra 3 at a substantial discount and do not need the Ultra 4’s longer battery life, new health sensing or extended workout modes.
You mainly want advanced health features in an everyday watch. The smaller Series 12 has the same new Health Sensing System and S11 chip for half the starting price.
You prefer a smaller or lighter watch. The Ultra 4’s 49mm case can feel bulky, especially for sleep tracking.
Our verdict: The Ultra 4 is worth buying if you will benefit from its 50-hour battery life, extended workout tracking or outdoor safety features. It also offers the Series 12’s new health sensing in a more rugged watch. For everyday use, the Series 12 offers better value; if you already own an Ultra 3, compare the cost of upgrading with how much its extra eight hours of rated battery life and new health features matter to you. 

							
		


Should I buy an older Apple Watch?

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The Series 11 and Ultra 3 are now the previous-generation models and may be good buys if retailers discount them enough. Before choosing any older Apple Watch, check both its price against the current model and whether it can run watchOS 27. The Series 9 and Ultra 2 are the oldest supported Apple Watch models models in their respective ranges; the SE 3 is the only supported SE.
The following models cannot install watchOS 27, so we would generally avoid buying them unless the price is exceptionally low and you are comfortable using older software:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
Start by comparing a discounted Series 11 with the Series 12, or an Ultra 3 with the Ultra 4. The Series 11 retains the Series 12’s 24-hour everyday battery rating but lacks its new Health Sensing System and Audio Intelligence features. The Ultra 3 retains satellite communication and dual-frequency GPS, but its rated battery life is 42 hours rather than the Ultra 4’s 50 hours. Series 10 and Ultra 2 can offer further savings if their price and battery condition make sense; Series 9 is the oldest standard model that runs watchOS 27.
What to look for when buying an older Apple Watch
Choose an S9 chip or newer for the longest software support.
Buy refurbished if possible. Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store includes a one-year warranty, while reputable third-party refurbishers can also offer good value.
Shop during major sales. Previous-generation Apple Watches often receive their biggest discounts during Prime Day and Black Friday.
Check the battery and Activation Lock. If you’re buying used, confirm the battery is in good condition, inspect the watch for damage, and make sure Activation Lock has been removed before you buy.

When is the best time to buy an Apple Watch?
The best time to buy an Apple Watch depends on whether you want the newest model or the lowest price.
The Series 12 and Ultra 4 are now on sale, alongside the SE 3. If you want the latest model and are happy with its price, you can buy now without an imminent replacement to worry about. If getting a discount matters more, compare retailers during the expected October sales and Black Friday in November.
The September launch also makes the Series 11 and Ultra 3 worth checking. Retailers may reduce remaining stock, but compare the actual saving with the features you would give up: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 add new health sensing, while the Ultra 4 also increases rated battery life from 42 to 50 hours.
Apple kept the new models’ starting prices at $399/£369 for Series 12 and $799/£749 for Ultra 4. Individual configurations and retailer prices vary.


						

							


When shouldn’t you buy an Apple Watch?
Avoid buying an Apple Watch:
Just before Apple’s annual September event, unless you need one immediately.
At full price when a major sale is only days away, such as Prime Day or Black Friday.
Without comparing prices. Check multiple retailers and use price-tracking tools such as CamelCamelCamel to avoid inflated “sale” prices.
If you’re paying extra for cellular but don’t need it. Cellular Apple Watch typically cost around $100 more and require a monthly data plan, while the GPS model offers better value for most people.
If battery life is your top priority. Apple Watch battery life still trails some competing smartwatches, so you may prefer an alternative platform if multi-day battery life is essential.

Where to find the best Apple Watch deals

				
					

				
			
IDG




Apple rarely discounts the Apple Watch itself, so the best deals are usually found at third-party retailers – we check these every month and record the best deals here: Top Apple Watch discounts & deals – Big savings on all models.
Best places to buy: Amazon is consistently one of the best places to find Apple Watch discounts, particularly during major sales. Other good options in the U.S. include Best Buy, Walmart, Target and Costco. In the U.K., check Amazon, Currys, Argos, John Lewis and KRCS.
Shop during major sales: The biggest discounts typically arrive during Amazon Prime Day (July and October) and Black Friday/Cyber Monday (November). Savings of $100–$150 on current-generation models are common. During Prime Day 2026, for example, the Apple Watch Series 11 fell to $279 ($120 off) and the Ultra 3 dropped to $649 ($150 off).
Check for education discounts: Students, teachers and education staff may qualify for discounted Apple Watch pricing through Apple’s Education Store U.S. (and Education Store U.K.). For more information read our guide to how to get a student discount at the Apple Education Store.
Tip: Before buying, compare prices across several retailers and check the recent price history with a tool such as CamelCamelCamel to make sure you’re getting a genuine deal rather than a temporary “discount” from an inflated price.


						

							


Is it worth buying a refurbished Apple Watch?
Buying a refurbished Apple Watch is another great way to save money, provided you buy from a reputable seller and choose a model that will continue to receive software updates.
Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store is the safest option. Every watch undergoes rigorous testing, cleaning and inspection, comes with a one-year warranty, includes new accessories, and is eligible for AppleCare. Apart from the plain white box, it’s difficult to tell the difference between a refurbished Apple Watch and a brand-new one. You can typically save around 15% on recent models, with even bigger discounts on older generations.
Check Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store or U.K. Refurbished Store for current models, configurations and prices. Stock changes regularly; compare any refurbished Series 11 or Ultra 3 with the price of a new Series 12 or Ultra 4 before buying.
The best Apple Watch refurbished deals: 
Apple’s U.S. Refurbished Store often has Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 3, SE 2, Ultra 2 and Ultra 3.
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for $339, $60 off
You may also find the Apple Watch Series 11, 10 and 9, SE 2, SE 3 and Ultra 3 at Apple’s U.K. Refurbished Store. 
Get a refurbished Apple Watch Series 11 for £309, £60 off
Third-party refurbishers can also offer excellent value, but quality varies. Terms such as “Excellent” or “Grade A”aren’t standardised, so always check the seller’s warranty, return policy and battery condition before buying. Be aware that Amazon Renewed devices, for example, aren’t refurbished to Apple’s standards and may not include a new battery or replacement parts.
The other key consideration is software support. Older Apple Watches eventually stop receiving new versions of watchOS, so avoid buying a model that’s nearing the end of its supported life. For the best balance of price and features, compare refurbished Series 11 and Ultra 3 models with the new generation first. Series 9, Series 10 and Ultra 2 can cost less and still run watchOS 27, but check their condition and savings carefully.
A refurbished Apple Watch can be one of the best values in Apple’s lineup – as long as you buy from a trusted seller and don’t choose a model that’s too old.
Read: Should I buy a refurbished Apple Watch? for more information.


						

							





 FAQ 


1.
Should I wait for the next Apple Watch?
You do not need to wait for 2026’s launch: the Series 12 and Ultra 4 went on sale in September 2026, and the SE 3 remains in Apple’s lineup. If you need a watch now, choose the model that fits your needs and budget. If you are mainly looking for a lower price, consider waiting for a sale or comparing discounted Series 11 and Ultra 3 stock. 
Apple has not announced when the next Apple Watch models will arrive, but we expect that the next update will happen in September 2027.





2.
How long does Apple support an Apple Watch?
Apple has traditionally supported Apple Watches with major watchOS updates for around five to six years, but that changed with watchOS 27, announced at WWDC 2026.
Apple dropped support for five older models in a single release:
Apple Watch Series 6 (2020)
Apple Watch Series 7 (2021)
Apple Watch Series 8 (2022)
Apple Watch SE (2nd generation, 2022)
Apple Watch Ultra (1st generation, 2022)
As a result, watchOS 27 only supports Apple Watches with an S9 chip or later, starting with the Apple Watch Series 9. While Apple may continue to provide security updates for older models for a limited time, they no longer receive new watchOS features.
The change makes software support a much more important consideration when buying an older or refurbished Apple Watch. If you want the longest possible lifespan, choose a model with an S9 chip or newer.





3.
Is the Apple Watch Series 11 still worth buying?
If it is substantially cheaper than the Series 12. Both have up to 24 hours of rated everyday battery life, but the Series 12 adds more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, a Readiness score and support for upcoming Audio Intelligence features, so be sure that you are willing to give those features up for the saving.

title: Apple Watch Ultra 2 vs. Ultra 4 Buyer's Guide: Should You Upgrade?
content:
The Apple Watch Ultra 4 arrives three years after the Ultra 2. Across those two generations, Apple added satellite connectivity, a larger display, new health sensors, and longer battery life. Are those changes enough to justify replacing an Ultra 2 or paying more for the newest model?


Both watches retain a 49mm titanium case, an Action button, a siren, a 3,000-nit display, dual-frequency GPS, and support for recreational diving to 40 meters. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 starts at $799 in the U.S. Apple has discontinued the Ultra 2, although its refurbished store currently lists it from $589. Here are the key differences between the two models:



Apple Watch Ultra 2
‌Apple Watch Ultra 4‌


LTPO2 OLED display with always-on
Wide-angle LTPO3 ‌OLED‌ display with 1Hz always-on refresh


410 by 502 pixels; 1,185 sq mm display area
422 by 514 pixels; 1,245 sq mm display area (5% larger)


S9 chip
S11 chip


2GB RAM
4GB RAM


Electrical heart sensor and third-generation optical heart sensor
Health Sensing System with new electrical and always-on optical heart sensors


Background heart-rate measurements
Background heart-rate measurements every five seconds


Heart-rate variability (HRV) measurements
More frequent measurements of overall HRV and Recovery HRV


Overnight Vitals view
Overnight and daytime Vitals views



Readiness app


Step tracking
More accurate all-day step tracking and a Steps watch-face complication


LTE and UMTS cellular connectivity
LTE and 5G cellular connectivity



Emergency SOS, Messages, and Find My via satellite



Audio Intelligence: Sound Recognition, automatic music identification, Live Rewind, and Siri Recap


Up to 36 hours of normal use
Up to 50 hours of normal use


Up to 72 hours in Low Power Mode
Up to 84 hours in Low Power Mode


Up to 12 hours of standard outdoor workout tracking
Up to 18 hours of standard outdoor workout tracking


Up to 17 hours of outdoor workout tracking in Low Power Mode with full GPS and heart-rate readings
Up to 25 hours in Extended Workout mode with full GPS and heart-rate readings


Up to 35 hours of outdoor workout tracking with fewer GPS and heart-rate readings
Up to 45 hours in Max Extended Workout mode, with GPS readings every second


Charges from 0 to 80% in about one hour
Charges from 0 to 80% in about 45 minutes


Natural titanium: 61.4 grams; black titanium: 61.8 grams
Natural titanium: 63.0 grams; black titanium: 63.1 grams


Dual-frequency GPS supporting GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, QZSS, and BeiDou
Dual-frequency GPS supporting GPS, Galileo, QZSS, and BeiDou


Now discontinued
Starts at $799




Is It Worth Upgrading From Ultra 2 to Ultra 4?

Most Apple Watch Ultra 2 owners should keep their watch if its battery still covers their usual days and workouts. It supports watchOS 27 and ‌Siri‌ AI, and continues to get new features through software updates.

The new Health Sensing System is the strongest reason to upgrade an Ultra 4. It measures heart rate every five seconds throughout the day and collects HRV data more frequently, enabling Recovery HRV, daytime Vitals, and the Readiness app. If you will use those insights to adjust your training or better understand changes in your daily condition, the ‌Apple Watch Ultra 4‌ offers a substantially improved health-tracking experience.

The S11 chip strengthens the case to upgrade. Alongside twice the memory, it enables more accurate all-day step counts, a Steps complication, and Audio Intelligence. Sound Recognition can alert you to important surrounding sounds on your wrist, while music recognition can identify songs automatically.

Satellite connectivity and longer battery life add further reasons to switch, especially if you spend time beyond cellular coverage or record long workouts. Apple's ratings increase from 36 to 50 hours of normal use and from 12 to 18 hours of standard outdoor workout tracking. The slightly larger display and faster charging are welcome improvements, but the new sensing and chip-enabled features make the bigger difference.

Should You Buy an Ultra 2 or Ultra 4?

For most people buying an Apple Watch Ultra now, future-proofing is the strongest reason to choose the latest model. Its S11 chip, 4GB of RAM, and Health Sensing System already enable Readiness, more detailed recovery metrics, and Audio Intelligence features. Live Rewind and ‌Siri‌ Recap are due later in 2026. If you plan to keep your watch for several years through successive software updates, that newer hardware makes the $799 model easier to justify.

title: Watch Steve Jobs defuse Apple’s Antennagate scandal in lost video footage
content:
Macworld





Back in July 2010, Apple was in crisis mode. Steve Jobs was sick. Gizmodo had just spoiled the launch of one the greatest iPhones ever made. And now headlines all over the web were bashing the iPhone 4 as having a serious antenna flaw.
It was so bad that Steve Jobs cut his vacation short and gathered members of the press for an impromptu conference on July 16 to explain the issue and field questions from the press. We’ve seen the video of the part where Steve Jobs shows off Apple’s antenna labs and equipment and explains the weak spots inherent to phones from that time, and announces a free case for every iPhone 4 user. He also announced Apple was extending its iPhone 4 return policy for 30 days.
At the conclusion of that presentation, Jobs said this:
“We love our users. And we try very hard to surprise and delight them… That’s what drives us, and when we have problems like this and when people are criticizing us, we take it really personally. Maybe we shouldn’t. Maybe we should have a wall of PR people. Keeping us away from all that, but we don’t…  But the data supports the fact that the iPhone 4 is the best smartphone in the world. And that there is no Antennagate. There is a challenge for the entire smartphone industry. To be able to improve its antenna performance someday to where there are no weak spots on any smartphone. And we’re dedicated to doing that.”
Following the 30-minute segment, he invited two of Apple’s lesser-known executives, CFO Tim Cook and Senior Vice President of Technologies Bob Mansfield, on stage to answer questions. They sat on stools on the stage and called on members of the press in the audience for 45 minutes. And oh boy is it worth watching.






Steve Jobs dominates the discussion with a masterful display of poise. He curses, he belittles, he jokes, and he seethes, but mostly, we get to watch Steve Jobs command the room and defuse what could have been a much larger scandal. He doesn’t just have an answer for every question, some of which are extremely inane. His answers are detailed, thoughtful, and remarkably insightful. A transcript doesn’t do it justice.
Take this exchange with Joshua Topolsky from Engadget, for instance:
Jobs: Can I replay your question back to you? 
Topolsky: Sure.
Jobs: You’re asking me, is there a software fix for smartphone attenuation that’s seen on almost every smartphone when you hold it in certain ways? Is that your question? 
Topolsky: In your phone. 
Jobs: So could we leap ahead of almost every smartphone that has attenuation when you hold it in certain ways by having better software on our phone? I’d love it.
Watching Steve Jobs barely crack a smile during the whole thing is just glorious to behold. Tim Cook speaks up a couple of times and Scott Forstall makes an impromptu appearance as well, but this is mostly a Steve Jobs masterclass. And we finally get to watch it.

title: How to remove Apple Intelligence models & reclaim storage in macOS 27
content:
Turning off Apple Intelligence in macOS 27 won't remove its downloaded models, but properly deleting the main model folder can free valuable internal SSD space. Here's how to do it.

macOS 27 introduces Siri AI
We're not fans of the fact that macOS can keep Apple Intelligence models on disk even after Siri AI is turned off. Apple doesn't provide a button for removing those downloaded files, so reclaiming the space requires going into Recovery and deleting the model folder directly.
This isn't an Apple-documented storage-management procedure, and the amount of space recovered can differ from the size macOS attributes to Apple Intelligence. In our test, the Mac started normally afterward and gained about 14 GB of available disk space.
Before the deletion, the Mac Storage pane attributed 27.59 GB to Apple Intelligence. Afterward, it showed 3.07 GB, and the Mac started normally. That 24.52 GB drop in the Storage category wasn't the same as the increase in available disk space.

title: iPhone 18 Pro review: The best kind of boring
content:
Macworld





At a glance
Expert's Rating



Pros
Crazy-fast performance
Better cooling performance
A “pro” camera that finally feels like it
Cons
The price went up
There are no major new features
The design is the same
Our Verdict 
It’s hard to get excited about a new iPhone that is just “the same thing but faster and with a slightly better camera,” especially when the iPhone Duo was announced at the same time. But the impressive A20 Pro performance and efficiency really help make this the iPhone Pro to beat all others.
Price When Reviewed
This value will show the geolocated pricing text for product undefined
Best Pricing Today




The iPhone 18 Pro is just like last year’s iPhone, but faster and with a slightly better camera. That’s it.
Back in the early iPhone days, we would call this an “S” model, because a year after the iPhone 4, there was the iPhone 4s. A year after the iPhone 5, the 5s. After the 6, the 6s. And each one was physically identical to its predecessor, but faster and with a somewhat better camera.
If you wanted to think of this as the iPhone 17 Pro S, you’d be spot on.
The thing about those “S” models is that, while they were kind of boring, they were still the best iPhones. So is it with this year’s model—there’s no incredible new feature or design change to get excited about, but that “same but better” formula results in one of the best iPhones in a long time.
The iPhone 17 Pro, but better
Last year, Apple introduced a new Cosmic Orange color for iPhone 17 Pro that shocked everyone with its boldness. It was an instant hit.
So it’s a little disappointing that the only thing visually different about the iPhone 18 Pro is that they got rid of Cosmic Orange and replaced it with Burgundy. Which is a fine color, but it’s no Cosmic Orange. There’s a black and a silver this year, along with a new pale blue called Glacier.

				
					

				
			
The iPhone 18 Pro, show in Glacier blue, is much more subdued than the ultra-bright 17 Pro

Foundry




Beyond the colors, you’d be hard-pressed to notice a difference between last year’s pro iPhones and this year’s. They have the same dimensions, though this year’s phones are just a touch heavier. They’re so similar that some cases for the iPhone 17 Pro or Pro Max will fit the iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max just fine. Certain other cases fit poorly because the camera plateau is about a half-millimeter taller on the new phones; it all depends on the design of the case.
You’ll also notice, when the iPhone is on, that the Dynamic Island cutout is just a little smaller, which leaves enough room for two dynamic activities to be tracked at once. Apple moved the IR sensor used with Face ID under the display and off to the side, behind a row of pixels with some sub-pixels removed and others made brighter to compensate. You can’t see it at all, and in my testing it seems to work just fine. But I also haven’t really found the smaller Dynamic Island has changed things much for me, either.
It’s what’s on the inside that makes the 18 Pro special: a new processor system and some camera improvements.
iPhone 18 Pro: A20 Pro performance
The A20 Pro is Apple’s first chip built on a 2nm process, and it’s seriously impressive. It’s not just the chip itself that makes the difference here; it’s what we might call the A20 Pro system. It involves a new packaging technique that puts the RAM off to the side of the chip for better cooling and an all new vapor chamber…also for better cooling.
It’s still a six-core CPU, but both the “Super” cores and the efficiency cores are improved, and the memory bus is 50 percent wider, providing 50 percent more bandwidth. The GPU is 7 cores, up for 6 in the A19 Pro, and also features architectural improvements. Take a look at these numbers.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




In the older Geekbench 6 test, single-core performance jumps an impressive 26 percent. The multi-core score is up even more at 30 percent higher. That’s a crazy jump for one year.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The more modern Geekbench 7 tests are also more strenuous, but the results are the same: a single-core score is 26 percent higher and a multi-core score is 28 percent higher.
Apple calls its big cores “desktop class” and that’s not just hype. This is single-core performance that is higher than an M5 and multi-core performance equal to an M3. In your phone. In your pocket. To put this CPU performance in context, this is a single-core score that beats the best Ryzen or Intel Core i7 desktop CPUs without exotic overclocking, and a multi-core score in the same range as most 8-core desktop CPUs from two or three years ago.
As impressive as the CPU is, the GPU seems to get an even bigger speed boost. Let’s take a lot at GPU performance for computational tasks (image segmentation, horizon detection, blurring backgrounds, face detection, and so on) using Geekbench 7’s GPU test.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




A 46 percent jump in GPU compute performance in a single year? It seems unthinkable, but Apple increased memory bandwidth by 50 percent and that is often a bottleneck for all kinds of graphics performance. For context, an M4 Mac scores around 54,000 in this test—13 percent slower. This is performance somewhere in-between the M1 Pro and the regular M5. In your pocket.
But that’s GPU compute. Surely when it comes to rendering complex 3D graphics like the kind used for high-end games, and stressing the CPU at the same time, the improvement isn’t as big? Think again.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Through several generations of 3DMark real-time graphics benchmarks, we see massive improvements with the A20 Pro. The relatively simple Wild Life Extreme test is 93 percent faster, almost twice as fast! The Solar Bay benchmark stepped up complexity and added some ray tracing elements, and the A20 Pro is 57 percent faster that last year’s A19 Pro. Steel Nomad Light is the heaviest test, though it doesn’t feature any ray tracing. It’s 53 percent faster.
This is graphics rendering performance that is faster than the M4 an an iPad Pro and almost as fast as an M5. Spot-checking with actual games, which are harder to benchmark in a deterministic fashion, we see a lot of the same results. Most games either just lock at 60 frames per second, or they’re anywhere from 40 percent faster to almost twice as fast.
The Neural Engine is more difficult to test, but the Geekbench AI benchmark affords us the ability to get a look at running machine learning routines on the Neural Engine alone if we want.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Most of the ML/AI code that runs on neural processing units (NPUs) are the lighter half-precision and quantized routines that demand quick results in a power-efficient way. The new Neural Engine has double the cores and runs these sorts of tasks more than 40 percent faster. Apple’s been steadily improving Neural Engine performance for years, but we usually see a 20-30 percent boost, not this.
Again, this is desktop-class stuff. An M5 doesn’t deliver scores like this, even. Apple doubled the Neural Engine cores in the M6, though, and that manages to pull ahead of the A20 Pro.
I’ve been testing and reviewing consumer tech for over 20 years, from early DIY gaming PCs through mobile technology and beyond. I’m not easily impressed by a year-over-year performance improvement. But the A20 Pro has me genuinely shocked. Single-core, multi-core, GPU, Neural Engine…it’s all drastically faster than the A19 Pro, which was already at the top of its class. In test after test, the A20 Pro delivers results that equal desktop-class chips of the sort you’d find in thin-and-light laptops bought in the last year or two.
iPhone 18 Pro: Camera improvements
For all the “pro” features Apple has added to the Pro iPhone cameras over the years — ProRAW photos, ProRES video, Dolby Vision, Genlock syncing, and so on — the actual photo-taking experience has felt decidedly point-and-shoot. If you wanted to take real control over your shots, you’d have to ditch the default Camera app and use a third-party app such as Halide or Blackmagic Camera.
This year, Apple has finally added what it calls “Pro controls” to the Camera app, which eliminates the need to use one of those apps for most photographers that want more than point-and-shoot style control. You get menus to adjust white balance, focus distance, shutter speed, and lens aperture, and can display a real-time histogram.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




It’s hard to believe that it took Apple this long to provide these basic manual controls, at least for the “Pro” iPhones. And it should be a scandal that they’re only available on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, instead of coming as a software update to earlier Pro models. There’s nothing about any of these controls, save for the aperture setting, that need to be exclusive to this year’s models. And indeed, most of them are alredy available on third-party apps.
About that aperture setting. It’s true, the main camera (and only the main camera) now has an adjustable physical aperture. It only has four settings: f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, and f/4. It defaults to f/1.8, which is a similar aperture wideness to earlier iPhones, and performs about the same. But it’s neat to see it move!

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The f/1.48 is wider and lets in more light, so it kicks in during low-light scenes, but an aperture that wide on a sensor this small results in slightly less sharp photos. So it wouldn’t be a good setting for a fixed-aperture lens on other iPhones, but it’s nice to have in a pinch.
Moving up to higher f-stop numbers makes the aperture smaller, which lets in less light and is more appropriate for bright daytime photography. It also makes the focus depth longer, so more of the background is in focus.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




Here’s an example. Focusing on the tree in the foreground, you can see the ladder in the background get a bit sharper as the aperture gets smaller. The effect is not dramatic; small sensors are less responsive to this sort of thing, and a maximum F-stop of 4 is still pretty wide. Most full-frame cameras have a maximum F-stop of at least F/16 or F/22. 
Users have complained for years now that Apple’s more recent image processing pipelines tend to make photos look worse than they did on older phones. The chief complaint seems to be oversaturation of colors and tone and a “plastic” effect that loses all grain and texture.
This year, Apple has tweaked its Photographic Styles setup yet again to give users more control over color temperature and tone. New this year is a “texture” setting that lets you increase or decrease fine texture detail or adjust the amount of skin smoothing or brightening.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




It’s another good attempt to bring some authenticity and humanity back into photos that, by their very nature, are very processed. I like it, but I think Apple may have been better off paying attention to the “Process Zero” fad sweeping the third-party camera apps lately, and provided a similar control of its own. Just a one-button, “minimal processing” setting that turns off all the AI help and gives you an authentic image, warts and all.
There a couple of other new tricks. A smart focus tracking feature lets you tap on an object and the focus will follow it as it moves. And Apple Reference Image, which signs individual pixels of the image and makes the original available all the time, to verify it has not been edited. You have to turn that on in Settings > Camera > Apple Reference Image, and then you have to take photos using the new Reference mode that appears. I suspect it won’t be used much outside of photojournalism.
Apple’s big advancement this year, the variable aperture camera, is a bit of a letdown. There’s just not enough aperture range for it to make a big difference with this small sensor. The new software controls, on the other hand, are very welcome and most of them should have been included on the Pro phones years ago. As much as I appreciate their inclusion in the standard Camera app today, I find it frustrating that Apple limits them to the iPhone 18 Pro for no good reason.
iPhone 18 Pro: Battery, charging, and thermal improvements
The A20 Pro’s performance is off-the-charts good, but it doesn’t suffer from poor efficiency at all. Quite the opposite. 
I used Geekbench 4’s battery benchmark, which runs sporadic tests in the background to keep the processor busy. It’s a more realistic and repeatable test than a typical video playback benchmark. (Dear Primate Labs: Please incorporate a new battery test in Geekbench 7!) I kept the display fixed at 200 nits of brightness, which is about midway on the brightness slider, and turned off all dynamic brightness and low-battery mode features.

				
					

				
			
Foundry




We’re looking at a 12 percent increase in battery life from last year’s model. The iPhone 18 Pro Max, which is identical in every way except size and battery, lasts an impressive 25 percent longer than the iPhone 17 Pro Max. It really is impressive to see how far iPhone battery life has come in just a few years. In three generations, Apple has more than doubled the real usable battery life of the iPhone Pro models.
It has sort of flown under the radar, but Apple improved charging speed this year as well. 

				
					

				
			
Foundry




The iPhone 18 Pro charges at a little bit higher rate from 0-80 percent, then sort of flatlines at around 10W or less for the rest of the charge curve. This gets it to 50 percent a few mintues faster than the iPhone 17 Pro, to 80 percent about 10 minutes faster, and to 100 percent almost 20 minutes faster.
It’s not a huge improvement, and it’s not as fast as the very fastest-charging Android phones, but it’s a noticeable improvement all the same.
Apple has made a big deal out of its new thermal solution, with a much bigger vapor chamber and a new chip packaging technique that moves the RAM to the side so it and the processor can be cooled more effectively. It’s a difficult thing to reliably test, but I can say from a year of experience with the iPhone 17 Pro that the iPhone 18 Pro definitely gets less hot. Playing certain games, recording extended video, and other long-term intensive tasks would often make the iPhone 17 Pro rather hot to the touch. I can’t claim that the 18 Pro stays cool in these same situations, but the heat buildup is very obviously less. 
Should you buy an iPhone 18 Pro?
The iPhone 18 Pro could truly be called the iPhone 17 Pro S. It looks and acts the same as last year’s flagship. The only really new features are a variable aperture feature that doesn’t really make that much of a difference and some really welcome Camera app upgrades that have been available in third-party apps for years, and have no real business being locked to the new phone.
The A20 Pro is a revelation. It’s a high high water mark for mobile performance and efficiency, with real speeds that push into laptop territory and even longer battery life than the very good battery life of last year’s iPhone. It’s a year-over-year performance leap we almost never see anymore.
But it doesn’t enable anything new. The phone looks the same, and most of the features are the same. There’s no special AI thing or awesome new capability you get with the iPhone 18 Pro that you don’t get with the iPhone 17 Pro (outside of the variable aperture and aforementioned photography features that other apps have).
So this year’s best iPhone is last year’s best iPhone, only more so. Much faster. Longer battery life. Faster charging. And a camera that’s just a bit better. Oh, and the price went up by $100, or $300 if you get the highest storage tiers. iPhone 17 Pro S indeed.

title: The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is so insane it’s worth waiting 4 months to get one
content:
Macworld





I recently reviewed the M5 Max Mac Studio, and it’s a powerhouse. But there’s a higher-end version that’s even more powerful. It’s the M5 Ultra Mac Studio, and our German colleagues at Macwelt have a full review of it. Macwelt shared their benchmarks with us, so here’s a look at the M5 Ultra Mac Studio and how it compares to the M5 Max and older Mac Studios.
The M5 Ultra tested here is the top-end chip configuration with a 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU. It also has a 4TB SSD and 256GB of RAM–the most you can get for now. Apple says that a 512GB option will be available in October. This model sells for $12,299 The 512GB model will likely cost an additional $5,000 or more.

Geekbench 7

		
			


Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.





The M5 Ultra has twice the CPU cores as the M5 Max in our tests. In general, the M5 Ultra offers a 47 percent increase in multi-core CPU performance over the M5 Max. Unsurprisingly, the single-core CPU results are basically the same, as is the case with all M-series generations.
Compared to the chip the M5 Ultra replaces in the Mac Studio lineup, it offers a 47 percent multi-core CPU boost. The M5 Ultra’s single-core CPU speeds are 27 percent faster.

Geekbench 6

		
			


Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.





The advantage of the M5 Ultra over the M5 Max in Geekbench 6 isn’t as drastic (25 percent) but that has more to do with the test than the chip. Geekbench 7 redesigned its multi-core tests and changed its workloads to better reflect real-world usage, so while this data point isn’t relevant anymore, it’s presented in case you’re curious. Geekbench 6 and 7 numbers are not comparable.

Cinebench 2026

		
			


Results are expressed as Cinebench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.





The M5 Ultra’s gigantic boost over the M5 Max is also seen here in Cinebench 2026–72 percent increase is huge. The GPU boost is significant, too, at 49 percent. Cinebench is more taxing than Geekbench by producing a high CPU load using Maxon’s Redshift render engine. If you work in media, pay attention to this result.

Blackmagic Disk Tests

		
			


Results are megabytes per second. Higher rates/longer bars are faster.




I said that the SSD performance was the big deal about the M5 Max Mac Studio, and it’s the same with the M5 Ultra model. You need a speedy SSD to complement the CPU performance.
One note about the SSD: Apple continues to outfit the Mac Studio with a removable SSD module. It’s a bit tricky to get inside the Mac Studio, take it apart, and upgrade the SSD yourself. But it can be done.

Geekbench AI Neural Engine

		
			


Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.





Geekbench AI GPU

		
			


Results are expressed as Geekbench scores. Higher scores/longer bars are faster.




The Geekbench AI results are interesting. The M5 Max and Ultra show a clear boost over older chips, but between the two chips themselves, there isn’t a difference except in the GPU Single Precision score. The M5 Ultra features a 32-core Neural Engine, twice the number of cores as the M5 Max. And the M5 Ultra has an 80-core GPU, twice that of the M5 Max.
The Mac Studio is popular with AI developers, and this test isn’t going to dissuade anyone. However, a recent report outlined Apple’s focus on local AI performance with the M7 chips, which are expected to be released next year. It’s just a rumor and we don’t even know if there will be an M7 Ultra, but it’s something AI developers will want to keep an eye on.
Obviously, you get a lot of processing power with the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. But is it worth its $10,000-plus price? If you’re willing to spend that much, almost certainly. There is a point where price is no object for performance–the horsepower investment will pay off. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio is the fastest Mac ever made by a pretty wide margin, and the price is commensurate. 
However, with orders already sliping into late January, if you want one, you’re going to want to get your order in pretty quickly.

title: How to upgrade your Mac mini without paying Apple’s sky high prices
content:
Macworld





The Mac mini boasts fast processors, and rivals even Apple’s most pro computers despite costing significantly less. However, as great as it is, there is a problem with the Mac mini—the at-purchase storage upgrades are super expensive and after you buy one, it’s nearly impossible to upgrade its internal components. However, we’re here to help.
There are two basic Mac mini models: the latest M4/M5/M6 mini (5 inches square, 2 inches deep) and older M1/M2 mini (7.7 inches square, 1.4 inches deep). Here, we have rounded up the best hardware upgrades and accessories you can buy for either the old or newer models. Most of the M1/M2 tips work with the Apple Studio, too, as that remains the same size.
Apple doesn’t let you upgrade the Mac mini with inexpensive third-party components such as RAM or internal storage, and it prices its custom-build options at the very high end of affordability. With the earlier Mac mini Apple fixed the RAM to the processor and the SSD to the logic board so they couldn’t be swapped out after you buy one. The M4/M4 Pro mini is different with a detachable SSD but swapping this out is beyond most mere mortals, and simply not possible with the M5/M6 Mac mini’s return to soldered NAND storage.
Here we look at your best Mac mini upgrade options, adding: storage, memory, screen, speakers and microphone. If you want to jump straight to the reviews:
Hubs and docks for new Mac mini
Hubs and docks for Mac mini M2
Other Mac mini accessories

				
					

				
			Above: Inside the Mac mini M4. Although it looks easy, because Apple’s SSD controller is built into the chip, you can’t simply swap out its SSD with a part bought from Amazon or some computer store. If you can do this yourself you probably wouldn’t be reading this article! And it’s impossible on the later M5/M5 Mac mini.L0vertodream via X
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding memory and storage
In our FAQ at the foot of this feature we go into more detail about the difficulties of upgrading the Mac mini’s internal components—as it is with most Macs. There are solutions that are quite messy, such as adding external storage. 

				
					

				
			Flexible but messy: A Mac mini with two external SSDs: a Plugable 1TB Thunderbolt 3 External SSD NVMe Drive and a CalDigit Tuff Nano (10Gbps USB-C). Thankfully there are less messy ways of adding fast storage to your Mac mini.
Foundry




Adding external storage
The simplest way to add storage to a Mac mini is the same as any other Mac: Connect an external hard drive or SSD using one of the Thunderbolt ports on the back of the computer. Even the slowest Solid-state drives (SSD) are faster than mechanical hard disk drives (HDD), but look out for speed differences—entry-level SSDs provide speeds of around 500MBps, while more advanced models can step up to 2,000MBps or even 6,000MBps. See SSD or HDD in the FAQs.
Another way to add inexpensive portable storage is via an SD or microSD card—once the go-to storage format for camera users but also a great format for cheap and portable backup and archive storage. Sadly, the Mac mini doesn’t have a card reader slot, so you’ll need to add one, such as this UGreen USB-C SD Card Reader for $15.
But these are admittedly ugly methods. You’ll have wires hanging out of the back of your Mac mini and a desk cluttered with drives. It’s neater to keep storage hidden inside. Apple won’t let you do it, but there are some great solutions that we have tested here.
Adding Internal storage
The best option is to get more internal storage in your Mac mini, but Apple’s custom-built pricing means upgrading a 256GB model to 1TB will cost you an extra $500, and 2TB will cost $1,000, while M5 Pro options cost even more: 4TB is $1,800 and 8TB will set you back a whopping $3,800.
If you can’t swing the prices for more storage or just decide later that you need more, there are hardware solutions that connect to the mini without messing up the footprint of the small computer. We’ve tested and reviewed these Mac mini storage accessories for you. The tested Mac mini hubs feature upgradeable and inexpensive internal storage plus a range of extra ports, supporting the NVMe form factors that resemble a stick of chewing gum.
Installing SSD into Mac mini hub or dock
Below we review the best Mac mini hubs and docks. Some include a hidden SSD enclosure where you can slot your own storage card with an included screwdriver and sometimes a thermal gel pad to transfer heat away from the drive and into the metal enclosure, preventing the SSD from overheating and suffering from thermal throttling.

				
					

				
			The Satechi CubeDock matched the latest Mac mini (M4/M5/M6) and hides its internal SSD slot under its base.
Simon Jary




For the M4/M5/M6 mini, there are SSD slots in the Ugreen 11-in-1 Mac mini Dock, Satechi CubeDock, Satechi Stand & Hub, and Orico MiniLink, reviewed below. Satechi has an M2 mini version of its Stand & Hub, and you can also choose the OWC ministack STX.
Installation is simple, with everything bar the SSD board itself included (screwdriver, screws, thermal gel pads). It’s a little fiddly but nothing to be worried about—if you can use a screwdriver, you can install the SSD board yourself.
SSD types: The docks and hubs we tested all take NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) M.2 SSDs, but check on the appropriate SSD size before investing in the SSD. Some take several lengths—for example 2230, 2242, 2260 and 2280—while others just fit the standard 2280. If that sounds scary, don’t worry as the 2280 is the most common SSD length.
SSD speeds: Note that the speed of the USB-C or Thunderbolt connection from the dock to the Mac mini will determine the data-transfer rate. A 10Gbps USB-C connection allows an SSD to achieve real-world transfer speeds of around 900 to 1,250 Megabytes per second (MBps). While 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 or USB4 pipes have a theoretical maximum of 5,000MB/s, protocol overhead and enclosure translation typically cap your speeds at around 3,000MBps. An 80Gbps connection (such as Thunderbolt 5) supports real-world SSD speeds of up to 7,000MBps.
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding ports and extra expansion
While the Mac mini has plenty of ports around the back, Apple includes just two USB-C to the front of the M4/M5/M6 mini, and did not bless the M2 Mac mini with any ports at the front at all. Alongside the SSD slots, all of the hubs and docks tested and reviewed here include an array of ports, including USB-A (missing from the M4 mini) and SD/MicroSD card readers (missing from the M2 and M4/M5/M6 Mac mini).
Thunderbolt, USB-C, Ethernet and HDMI are all included in the Mac mini. Having access to more Thunderbolt or USB-C is useful, especially if powered. Some docks feature faster Ethernet.
USB-A is the legacy port missing from the Mac mini M4, used mainly for flash drives, memory sticks and older devices. This has largely been replaced with USB-C, but having at least one at your disposal can be handy.
SD card readers are also missing from the Mac mini, and are an affordable way of adding ultra-portable storage cards, which are cheaper—but slower—than SSDs. You can buy a SanDisk memory card with 512GB of storage for under $100.
Another port-adding option is to buy yourself a Thunderbolt hub, such as the 40Gbps CalDigit Thunderbolt 4 Element Hub that features four 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 ports (including one side-mounted upstream to the computer), four 10Gbps USB-A ports, and a power supply. The Element 5 Hub from the same company offers four Thunderbolt 5, two 10Gbps USB-C and three 10Gbps USB-A ports. We’ve tested the best Thunderbolt hubs and docks if you want even more ports than that. Granted, they won’t be as neat as the dedicated Mac mini docks and hubs reviewed here, but there are tons of options out there.
Best Mac mini hubs and docks
The criteria we used for the products reviewed below was that they had to fit the Mac mini and connect to it without ruining the Apple aesthetic or the Mac mini’s compact footprint. We tested the following docks and hubs with the Apple Mac mini (M4/M5/M6 models).

As a Thunderbolt 5 docking station it works best with the 80Gbps Mac mini M4/M5 Pro but will work well with the 40Gbps mini M4. Underneath the dock there’s a hatch that when removed reveals a slot for an SSD drive of up to 8TB. It supports 2280 and shorter 2230/2242/2260 M.2 NVMe SSD sizes (PCIe 4×4), and delivers up to 6000MBps in data transfer speed. Satechi even includes a visual SSD installation guide in the CubeDock’s packaging.

There’s not as many ports here as on the CubeDock reviewed above but there’s still plenty to add to the Mac mini’s own, including two USB-C rather than just focusing on USB-A like some Mac mini hubs do. The Satechi CubeDock”s two USB-A ports should be plenty enough for most people but Ugreen includes five, which seems like overkill.
There’s an SSD slot that takes M.2 NVMe SSDs of types 2230/2242/2260/2280, with a maximum capacity of 8TB. You’re advised to connect to a wall charger to keep the SSD working to its peak performance.
The two card readers at the front of the dock support ultra-portable SD and MicroSD cards. You could just use these for backup storage, but at 104MBps UHS-I they are probably too slow to work directly from while the dock’s internal SSD supports up to 10Gbps.

The Orico MiniLink gives you the requisite USB-A ports and fast card readers missing from the Mac mini. Where it differs from the other docks and hubs reviewed here is its dual SSD slots, meaning you can add up to 16TB of fast storage in the two bays.
One slot is rated at around 3000MB/s and the other around 1300MB/s because the faster slot has more USB4 bandwidth available. Start with an affordable drive today and add another later without replacing it, or dedicate one SSD to active projects and the other to backups, media libraries or archived files. 16TB of storage could set you back as much as $3,000, so you might pick this dock for the flexibility of two slots rather than the massive potential capacity.

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary


There are two basic models of MiniLink: the dual-SSD 40Gbps M47P and a 10Gbps one-slot M49P that has a couple of extra audio ports but slower card readers. Mae sure you chose the correct model because the company’s online store can be confusing as are its Amazon listings.
In testing, we did find the active cooling fan quite noisy. In a busy environment it can be ignored but if you need silence at least the MiniLink has a front-mounted power button.

Foundry





 FAQ 


1.
Can you upgrade the Mac mini hard drive?
It is possible to swap out the internal SSD on some Mac mini models (M4/M4 Pro) but you’ll need to be very tech-savvy. You have to carefully pry open the bottom cover, remove the internal fan, swap the SSD module using Torx bits, and use a second Mac via DFU mode to restore the operating system. Note that opening the chassis voids your Apple warranty and risks damaging delicate internal connectors. Instead, we recommend you look at the add-on solutions reviewed here.
Apple soldered the solid-state drive (SSD) directly onto the logic board of the older M1/M2 and M5/M6 Mac mini models when you chose the capacity at the point of purchase. While it is not possible to later upgrade the drive, you can add extra SSDs or hard-disk drives (HDD) via accessories.





2.
Can you upgrade the Mac mini memory?
Apple builds the RAM directly as part of the processor of the Mac mini (unified memory architecture) when you choose the amount of memory at the point of purchase. It is not possible to later upgrade the RAM, so you must choose the most you are likely to need when buying the computer.





3.
SSD or HDD?
Solid-state drives (SSD) have no moving parts. Data is stored on interconnected flash memory microchips, which allows for data to be pulled from many different places at once and significantly increases memory read speeds. Hard disk drives (HDD) rely on spinning metal disks to read and write data.
Most of the solutions reviewed here are focused on the faster NVMe type of SSD that speed up boot times, improve the responsiveness of your programs, and generally make your computer feel faster. However, you’ll pay more money for the same storage capacity on SSDs as HDDs. SSDs cost more per gigabyte than mechanical HDDs and aren’t often available in ultra-high capacities. Even as prices of SSDs continue to drop, HDDs will always be cheaper.





4.
Upgrading the Mac mini: Adding faster ethernet
One of the build-to-order options offered by Apple is to upgrade the Mac mini’s ethernet from 1 Gigabit to 10 Gigabit (an extra $100). As with the RAM and storage, once you’ve picked your Ethernet speed, there’s no way to upgrade the internal connector later. But you can buy adapters quite cheaply. Cable Matters sells a 10G Ethernet Adapter for around $89 if you suddenly need faster network access after you’ve purchased your Mac mini. Ugreen has 2.5GbE and 5GbE adapters that connect to one of your Mac’s USB-C or Thunderbolt ports.





5.
Does the Mac mini see an SSD in a dock as internal or external storage?
An SSD installed inside a dock is still external storage from the Mac’s perspective.

title: Meta Did a 'One More Thing' and It's an AI Tamagotchi
content:
Apple has reportedly shelved plans to launch an AI pendant, while Meta appears to be going all out in the nascent hardware space with a new handheld AI companion. Mark Zuckerberg used his "one more thing" moment at the company's annual Connect event on Wednesday to unveil the Muse Charm, a puck about the size of an Apple Watch featuring a tamagotchi-like, interactive avatar that can be used to chat with the company's Muse AI.

"Muse Charm is a delightful and fun device built for you to talk and interact with your Muse. It brings the power of Muse with a state of the art real-time voice model into a device that fits in your pocket. 

"We packed the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to. You just go ahead and tap here in the fingerprint sensor in the corner, and you can start talking without having to unlock a phone or open an app.

"So if you're not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what's going on around you."

That's all we got about the device, which Meta is aiming to have on sale by the holiday season. 

Otherwise, Connect was mostly about the company's new Meta VR Glasses. They have a tethered puck for the storage and battery, and the headset is five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3 at 100 grams, with full-color passthrough video support and a 5K display. (For context, M5 Apple Vision Pro weighs 750–800 grams depending on the configuration.)


Meta says the glasses will offer "cinema-grade clarity" with support for Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos spatial audio, and they can deliver up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback on a single charge. 

The device runs every game available for Quest headsets, and supports Xbox Cloud Gaming. You can also connect it to a PC or Mac and control things with a virtual keyboard and trackpad on a desk. Meta VR Glasses are set to launch in the spring with a $1,300 starting price.


Meanwhile, in an apparent bid to throw off the "pervert glasses" label, Meta also announced an audio-only version of its Ray-Ban smart glasses. The new model supports media playback and calls, and runs for up to 12 hours on a single charge, while the charging case adds up to 48 hours of battery life. Pre-orders are open and the glasses ship on October 13, starting at $349.

Meta hasn't abandoned its camera-equipped Ray-Ban smart glasses, though. Far from it. The company is refreshing its Ray-Ban Meta with a slimmer design and a button that activates Meta AI. The third-generation model is said to have a longer nine hours of battery life (versus eight on the second-gen model) and a new six-microphone array that the company says can cut out over 90 percent of background noise. The 12MP camera supports 3K video capture, with Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio support coming soon. There are multiple styles to choose from, and prices start at $449.

I wanted to comment on the aspect ratio of the Duo’s outer and inner screens – both about 1.4 : 1. As an ex-graphic designer, this ratio (known as the silver ratio, 1 to the square root of 2) is very well known to me. That is because in the UK and Europe all our paper sizes are based on this ratio. 
A4 is 297 x 210mm which when folded exactly in half results in A5, which has the same ratio. This continues with smaller sizes of A6, etc. Going the other way, A3 is double A4, etc, until you get to A0, which has a surface area of 1 metre squared. Neat eh? 
The iPhone Duo therefore is like an A5 sheet of paper, folded in half when closed, and is something that will have been very familiar with Molly Anderson who (like Jony Ive) is from the UK.

title: iPhone Handoff in iOS 27: How It Works, Pricing, and Carrier Support
content:
Apple in iOS 27 introduced iPhone Handoff, a new eSIM feature that allows you to use the same number on two iPhones and seamlessly swap between them. The number is only active on one iPhone at a time, so it's not like having two independently active lines. 


It's also different from Apple's existing Handoff feature for continuing an app task on another Apple device. Here's what you need to know about the new iPhone Handoff feature.

What Moves Between the Two iPhones?

When you switch phones with iPhone Handoff, your calls, voicemail, messages (including iMessage, RCS, SMS, and MMS) and Find My location move to the active iPhone. You'll see a "Switched to this iPhone" message on the screen to confirm the change. 

Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices, and third-party apps work across both devices, though some third-party apps may require a separate sign-in or take time to sync. Any banking apps you use may also ask you to approve access on the other device.

What Do You Need for iPhone Handoff?

Both iPhones must be running iOS 27 or later. They'll also need to be:
Connected to Wi-Fi

Sharing the same Apple Account

Using Messages in iCloud for messages sync

Signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account
iPhone Handoff works with Dual SIM as long as both eSIMs are from carriers that support iPhone Handoff. Both eSIMs must be set up for iPhone Handoff separately, one at a time. Once set up, both eSIMs switch together simultaneously when you unlock your iPhone.

Which Carriers Support iPhone Handoff?

iPhone Handoff is available through T-Mobile in the United States and Telekom in Germany. Verizon (U.S.) and EE (U.K.) will support iPhone Handoff later this year.

AT&T has so far not committed to supporting iPhone Handoff, with a company spokesperson recently pointing to the carrier's existing eSIM activation and transfer options instead.

How Much Does iPhone Handoff Cost?

T-Mobile is charging customers $5 per month to use iPhone Handoff. 

In Germany, Deutsche Telekom is charging €6.95 per month for iPhone Handoff, but only on plans that do not already include multi-SIM functionality. An added multi-SIM costs €6.95 per month (one is included with the current MagentaMobil L plan and two with XL).

No other carriers have announced pricing yet.

How Do You Set It Up?

iPhone Handoff can be enabled when setting up a new iPhone. At the "Set Up Cellular" screen, choose "Use Number on This iPhone and Another," then follow the prompts on both phones.

Settings ➝ Cellular on the phone you want to add. Tap Set Up Cellular or Add eSIM, choose Use Number on This iPhone and Another, and follow the prompts. You then get to choose which device is your main iPhone (ideally, the one you use most often) and which is your secondary iPhone. 


After setup, unlock either phone to make your number active on it.

What Should You Know Before Switching?

If you have an Apple Watch, it won't switch its pairing to the other device when your phone number moves, so make sure you pair it with the iPhone you expect to use most. Also, some Wallet items, including certain transit passes and IDs, may only work on one device at a time.

Carrier account management and some services like Call Forwarding and Caller ID will remain tied to your main iPhone. 

Can I Replace an iPhone That Uses iPhone Handoff?

Yes, but you need to transfer the eSIM from either iPhone to the replacement device. The below steps should be followed while your new iPhone is placed next to your existing devices that use iPhone Handoff. 

 
On your new iPhone (replacement), open the Settings app.

 
Tap Cellular and then tap Set up Cellular or Add eSIM.

 
Select an iPhone and tap Continue.

 
Tap Transfer. (If your carrier doesn't support eSIM transfer from a companion iPhone, you must enroll in iPhone Handoff again: On your iPhone that you are transferring the eSIM from, tap Continue, and follow the onscreen prompts.)

 
Tap Continue.

 
Follow the onscreen prompts on both devices.

The eSIM will deactivate on the old iPhone you transferred from.

What If I Want to Stop Using iPhone Handoff?

If you want to stop using iPhone Handoff at any time, you need to contact your carrier. Simply deleting an eSIM from your iPhone may not stop the carrier from charging you for the service.

title: ChatGPT in Siri 'Persistently Underperforming,' Says OpenAI
content:
OpenAI saw disappointing results working with Apple to integrate ChatGPT in Siri, according to court documents filed [PDF] in its ongoing legal fight with Elon Musk's company SpaceXAI (xAI at the time the lawsuit was filed).


Apple added ChatGPT to ‌Siri‌ in December 2024, but users had to go through a multistep opt-in process, which added a layer of friction. By January 2025, OpenAI said the integration was "off to a slow start" and the company cut its forecast for the number of incremental logged-in weekly active users that it expected to get from the partnership.

Much of the filing is redacted, but OpenAI said that by the time Musk's companies filed an antitrust lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI, "it was clear that Apple's integration of ChatGPT was dramatically underperforming." In a later section of the filing, OpenAI said again that the Apple integration was "persistently underperforming," leading to a March 2026 conversation between Apple and OpenAI that is redacted.

OpenAI asked Apple for a two-year exclusivity period, but Apple refused. The agreement between the two companies explicitly said the deal was non-exclusive and Apple had the right to "integrate products or services that provide the same or similar functionality as [ChatGPT]." Apple told OpenAI that it planned to integrate one provider and then add more, and it made similar statements publicly when announcing the feature. Apple also signed a deal with Google, and Apple's newest models are based on Gemini.

OpenAI's filing disputes many of the claims in the xAI lawsuit. Musk alleged OpenAI and Apple had an exclusive deal and that the agreement harmed xAI's growth and customer acquisition. OpenAI says the contract proves there was no exclusive deal, and even if there were, xAI can't prove harm because the ChatGPT ‌Siri‌ integration just didn't draw many new ChatGPT users.
Even if the Court assumes that Apple users who elect to use ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence are foreclosed from OpenAI's rivals (which they are not), the amount of foreclosure caused by the Agreement is indisputably de minimis. While Plaintiffs' experts declined to calculate foreclosure shares, OpenAI's expert, Dr. Catherine Tucker, calculated the share of GenAI consumers who accessed ChatGPT through Apple Intelligence across multiple metrics using the same data and market definition relied upon by Plaintiffs' experts. On these assumptions, Dr. Tucker found foreclosure shares of [REDACTED] across all metrics, consistent with OpenAI's internal view that Apple Intelligence saw minimal usage.

Musk's companies dropped their claims against Apple earlier this month, leaving OpenAI as the sole defendant in the lawsuit. OpenAI's filing asks the court to toss out xAI's claims prior to the trial planned for January 2027.

title: You Can Now Try Apple's Unreleased Copland OS in Your Browser
content:
In the mid–1990s, Apple worked on an operating system called Copland, which was announced but never commercially released because of project management issues and feature creep. Parts of Copland were eventually included in Mac OS 7.6 and Mac OS 8, but it was so problematic as a whole that Apple nixed it before it was finished.


Michael Steil, who works to reverse engineer vintage hardware and software, was recently able to get Copland running in emulation. He modified the open-source Power Mac emulator DingusPPC, and he said it took 11 patches to get Copland up and running. He has a browser version of Copland you can try on his website, and shared the patches needed to boot Copland.

During Copland's development, Apple released three beta versions. The last beta was D11E4, which is what Steil got to work. He said Copland is "notoriously hard to run on real hardware," and wasn't previously available in emulation.
