title: The new Mac mini hides an ugly SSD secret
content:
Macworld





The good news about the new Mac mini is that it offers very good CPU and GPU performance, whether it’s the M6 or M5 Pro model. But there is some bad news under the hood: Apple has returned to using soldered-on SSDs, which means owners can’t upgrade the storage themselves.
Expand Mac mini took apart the M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini and found the soldered SSD. It’s an unexpected turn, since the previous M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini switched to an SSD design that was implemented as a removable module. As such Expand Mac mini and others made a business out of selling SSD module upgrades. 


Mac mini M6 / M5 Pro have updated design to have the SSD NANDs soldered onto the motherboard 🫠
Not what we are hoped for!https://t.co/SF5v8Acw8I pic.twitter.com/rkbnT1kVhV
— Expand Mac mini (@expandmacmini) September 22, 2026





It gets even worse with the M6 Mac mini. If you look at the pictures in Expand Mac mini’s post above, you can see the SSD module at the bottom of the Mac. The M6 Mac mini pictured is the model with a 256GB SSD, and it’s a single module. As we’ve seen before, having two SSD modules is better for speed. The single module means it’s going to be significantly slower, though users can upgrade to the 512GB model to get the dual design.
The M4 Mac mini was something of an outlier for the Mac mini with an upgradable SSD.  If you were going to buy a Mac mini and held out for the new one, you could try to find a used M4 Mac mini for sale, but given the Mac mini’s stock issues, you’ll probably end up paying more than you should (and Apple’s Certified Refurbished Store does not have any in stock).
It’s still possible to upgrade your Mac mini without paying Apple’s sky high prices by adding these Mac mini-specific accessories.
Everyday Mac mini buyers probably won’t notice either of these downgrades, but the Mac mini has become very popular among AI enthusiasts, who won’t be happy about the changes. They’ll be happy to know that the M5 Max and Ultra Mac Studio still has an upgradeable SSD. However, that model costs a lot more than the Mac mini.

title: iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e: Release date, rumored specs, price, cameras, and latest news
content:
Macworld





For years, Apple has followed a predictable iPhone launch schedule, introducing new iPhones in September – the standard model and the Pro model. In the spring, Apple often releases a less expensive phone – previously the “SE” iPhones and, more recently, the “e” series.
Apple has now split the iPhone 18 launch. It unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and foldable iPhone Duo in September 2026, without announcing a standard iPhone 18 or iPhone 18e. Reports point to a spring 2027 launch for the less expensive models, but Apple has not confirmed either phone or a release date.
So, what can we expect from the iPhone 18 and 18e? Detailed specifications are scarce, but there are indications that the iPhone 18 may face some compromises. 
Below is a log of what we’ve heard so far about the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, based on the most recent and reliable rumors, analyst reports, and leaks, along with historical precedent.
iPhone 18 vs 18e rumors at a glance

Did Apple launch the iPhone 18 in September?
No. Apple’s September 9 event came and went without an iPhone 18 or 18e. The company announced the iPhone 18 Pro, Pro Max and iPhone Duo instead. The standard and lower-cost models are rumored for spring 2027, although Apple has not confirmed that timetable.
The new split-release strategy may make Apple’s increasingly large iPhone lineup easier to manufacture, while giving its premium models the spotlight during the crucial fall launch period.
It would also create a second major iPhone launch window in spring, when the iPhone 18 is expected to arrive alongside the iPhone 18e and Air 2. There is a separate rumor that the Air 2 could effectively become the iPhone 18, but that claim remains fairly speculative at this stage.


						

							


When will the iPhone 18 and 18e release?
iPhone 18: Expected in spring 2027 with an A20 chip, rumored to have more RAM and cameras, the iPhone 18 could even disappear entirely if Apple turns the thinner dual-camera Air 2 into its standard iPhone.
iPhone 18e: The iPhone 18e is expected in spring 2027 rumored to have an A20 chip, 9GB RAM and a C2 modem, while retaining a single 48MP rear camera.
While Apple has launched its standard and high-end iPhone models together ever since the first Pro phone arrived in 2019, this year looks to be different. Apple launched the iPhone 18 Pro models in September 2026 without a standard iPhone 18. Reports now point to a spring 2027 launch for the standard model, which would leave the iPhone 17 on sale for roughly 18 months before its replacement.
So if you bought an iPhone 17 at launch and are looking to upgrade, you’ll either need to spring for an iPhone 18 Pro or wait until March or April when Apple may hold a second iPhone event or at least launch the new iPhones via press release.
We also expect Apple to release the iPhone 18e and iPhone Air 2 at the same time – although there is a rumor that the iPhone 18 might actually be the iPhone Air 2.
“Early Apple” published a claim on X that Apple is “exploring the idea” of calling what is essentially the iPhone Air 2 the ‌iPhone 18‌ rather than launching a third device. In July Jon Prosser made a similar suggestion in a FTP video that Apple could eventually streamline the lineup around the iPhone, iPhone Pro and iPhone Duo, with the Air serving as a stepping stone toward that strategy.


						

							


What the iPhone 18 Pro launch revealed about the iPhone 18
The iPhone 18 Pro’s A20 Pro chip gives us our first look at this generation of Apple silicon. 
It does not confirm the standard A20’s specifications though. We still don’t know how much RAM the iPhone 18 or 18e will have, or which Pro features will be available with the cheaper phones. 


						

							







What specs will the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e have?
Apple has introduced the A20 Pro chip in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The iPhone 18 and 18e are expected to use a standard A20, although Apple has not announced that chip. Like A20 Pro, the standard chip could use a 2-nanometer manufacturing process, but its specifications remain unknown.
The A20 may retain the A19’s six-core CPU while improving performance and efficiency. A five-core GPU is possible for the iPhone 18, with a reduced configuration potentially reserved for the 18e. Those are predictions based on Apple’s existing chip lineup, rather than confirmed details. We also expect improvements to on-device AI processing, although the standard A20 may differ substantially from A20 Pro, which has a Dual 16-core Neural Engine.
The standard iPhone 18 is rumored to have more RAM than the iPhone 17’s 8GB. Analyst Jeff Pu has predicted 12GB, while Ming-Chi Kuo has suggested an unusual 9GB configuration for both the iPhone 18 and 18e. Given rising memory costs, we consider 9GB plausible, but there is no agreement yet on how much memory either phone will have.
The amount of RAM could affect more than multitasking. Apple already reserves some iOS 27 features – including customizable Siri voice expressivity and pace, and more accurate on-device dictation – for iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. That makes feature support an important question for the iPhone 18 and 18e. Apple has not said whether 9GB or 12GB of RAM determines eligibility for those features, so we cannot assume that either phone will include or miss out on them.
Apple has also introduced its C2 cellular modem in the iPhone 18 Pro. Apple says it supports mmWave in the U.S., delivers faster uploads than C1X and uses 15 percent less energy. The iPhone 18 and 18e may adopt C2, but Apple has not confirmed their modems. Both could also use Apple’s N1 wireless chip, which supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and Thread, though that remains a prediction for the unannounced phones.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18 and 18e’s cameras be improved?

				
					

				
			iPhone 17e camera. 
David Price / Foundry





24MP selfie camera on iPhone 18
iPhone 18e may retain a 12MP selfie camera
48MP Main cameras expected
Revised Camera Control button on iPhone 18
The iPhone 18 could get another front-camera upgrade. Apple introduced an 18MP Center Stage camera with the iPhone 17 generation, but reports now suggest the standard iPhone 18 will move to a 24MP selfie camera. That should potentially deliver more detail and give Apple more resolution to work with for cropping and computational photography.
The rumor that the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 could be one and the same may mean that the iPhone Air gets a second rear camera. 
The situation with the iPhone 18e is less clear. While some rumors have suggested that 24MP cameras could spread across the wider iPhone 18 family, a November 2025 J.P. Morgan report said the lower-cost iPhone 18e will retain a 12MP front camera. For now, we wouldn’t assume that the 18e will get the same selfie-camera upgrade as the iPhone 18.
There has been much less information about the rear cameras. The current iPhone 17 has 48MP Main and 48MP Ultra Wide cameras, while the iPhone 17e has a single 48MP Main camera. We therefore expect the iPhone 18 to retain two 48MP rear cameras and the iPhone 18e to continue with a single 48MP Main camera, although there haven’t yet been reliable reports of major sensor upgrades for either model.
Apple may also simplify Camera Control. According to Weibo leaker Instant Digital, the iPhone 18’s button will retain pressure sensitivity but drop the capacitive sensing used by current models, potentially reducing complexity and cost. The iPhone 18e isn’t expected to gain Camera Control.


						

							


Will the iPhone 18e get a display upgrade?

				
					

				
			iPhone 17e display.
David Price / Foundry




The iPhone 18 is likely to use a display similar to the iPhone 17, with up to 1,000 nits of typical SDR brightness, 1,600 nits peak HDR brightness, and up to 3,000 nits outdoors.
The iPhone 18e could get a more noticeable upgrade, although reports remain inconsistent. The current iPhone 17e uses an older display with relatively modest brightness and a notch rather than Dynamic Island. Some reports suggest the iPhone 18e will finally move to a newer panel with Dynamic Island, potentially bringing it closer to the iPhone 15, which offered up to 2,000 nits of outdoor brightness. However, the Dynamic Island upgrade remains disputed.
What does appear more likely is that Apple will continue to limit the 18e to a 60Hz display. According to Digital Chat Station, the phone will retain a 60Hz LTPS OLED panel rather than adopting the LTPO technology used for ProMotion. That would mean no 120Hz ProMotion refresh rate or Always-On display, even as those features become more widespread elsewhere in the iPhone lineup.


						

							


How much will the iPhone 18 and 18e cost?
Following the iPhone 18 Pro launch in September, Apple increased the price of the iPhone 17 from $799 to $899 and the iPhone 17e from $599 to $699 in the U.S. 
The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max launched at $1,199 and $1,299 respectively, also reflecting a $100 increase over their predecessors. 
Rising DRAM and NAND costs may help explain the increases, although Apple has not attributed these specific iPhone price changes to a single cause. 
There may be further pressure on 2027 prices. DigiTimes reports that Apple has accepted higher prices from Samsung for memory supplied in early 2027. That could make it harder for Apple to hold the iPhone 18 and 18e at the current models’ starting prices.
Will Apple increase prices further when the new models launch? Rising component costs could also affect the iPhone 18 and 18e, but it is too early to say whether Apple will raise their prices, or by how much.


						

							


Should you wait for iPhone 18?
If you want a Pro iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are available now. If you prefer a standard or lower-cost model and your current phone is serving you well, you could wait: the iPhone 18 and 18e are rumored to arrive in spring 2027, although Apple has not confirmed either launch.
There’s no need to wait if you need a phone now. We still recommend the iPhone 17 and 17e, which start at $899 and $699 respectively. 
If price is your main concern, look for discounts during Amazon’s October sale and Black Friday. You may also find a worthwhile deal sooner, particularly from a retailer or through a carrier offer. Read: When is the best time to buy a new iPhone?

title: iPhone Air vs. iPhone 18 Pro Buyer's Guide: Which Should You Buy?
content:
The iPhone Air and iPhone 18 Pro are just $100 apart at Apple's current prices, but they offer different advantages. The Air puts a 6.5-inch display in an exceptionally thin, light body. The newer Pro adds a more versatile camera system, longer battery life, and faster performance.


The iPhone Air launched in 2025 at $999, but Apple now sells the 256GB model for $1,099. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199 for the same storage capacity, while the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max starts at $1,299. Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these iPhones is best for you.

At Apple's current prices, the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ is clearly the stronger choice for most buyers. The ‌iPhone Air‌ makes a stronger case in the hand than it does on a specification sheet. It is 46 grams lighter than the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌, has a slightly larger display, and feels unlike any other iPhone. With its polished titanium frame and frosted glass back, it looks more classy and premium than the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ in many respects. If appearance, thinness, weight shape how much you enjoy using a phone every day, choosing the Air can be worthwhile despite its camera, speaker, and battery limitations. The Pro Max offers a 6.9-inch screen and even longer battery life, but weighs 84 grams more than the Air.

unlocked 256GB model for $899.99 earlier this year. If you find a new ‌iPhone Air‌ for around $900 while the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ remains $1,199, the roughly $300 saving makes the Air much more compelling if you can live with one rear camera and shorter battery life.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman expects the next ‌iPhone Air‌ in spring 2027, and an Ultra Wide camera has reportedly reached advanced testing. Analyst Jeff Pu expects a smaller Dynamic Island and A20 Pro chip. Separately, leaker "Digital Chat Station" has claimed it will have a 3,500mAh battery, up from the current model's 3,149mAh, while The Information has reported that it could gain vapor chamber cooling. If the current Air's camera, battery life, or sustained performance gives you pause, waiting could address those concerns; a steep discount is more persuasive if the current model already meets your needs.

title: Apple’s Back to School deal ends September 24 in the U.S. – U.K. offer continues
content:
Macworld





Apple runs an annual education promotion traditionally known as its “Back to School” sale. In 2026, Apple calls it the “College Student Offer” in the U.S. and the “University Student Offer” in the U.K. Eligible buyers include higher education students, parents buying for them and education staff; the offer does not cover parents buying for school-age children.
The promotion adds an incentive to Apple’s year-round education prices on qualifying Macs and iPads. Previous offers have included AirPods, Apple Pencils and other accessories. This year, eligible purchases come with an Apple Gift Card worth up to $150 in the U.S. or £120 in the U.K.
The U.S. promotion began on July 16. Apple originally set an August 27 end date, but extended the offer to September 24, 2026. So if you want to take advantage you will need to act quickly. 
The U.K. promotion began on August 13 and runs until October 22, 2026.


Region2026 Start date2026 End Date2026 Deal

North AmericaJuly 16, 2026September 24, 2026 (extended)Confirmed: Gift cards worth up to $150
U.K. & Europe August 13, 2026October 22, 2026Confirmed: Gift Cards worth up to £120.
Australia January 7, 2026March 11, 2026Ended: Free/discounted AirPods, Apple Pencil, Keyboards and Mice

 



Read on to find out everything you need to know about Apple’s Higher Education promotion this year, including when it is expected to begin in your region, what products and incentives may be included, who qualifies, and how to take advantage of the offer.
Apple’s “Back to school” deal: At a glance
What is Apple’s “Back to School” deal? The 2026 deal is gift cards worth up to $150/£120 with purchases of qualifying Macs and iPads.
When is Apples “Back to School” deal? It is running from July 16 to September 24, 2026 in North America. In the U.K. and Europe it is running from August 13 to October 22.
Is this the only student saving from Apple? No, Apple offers a discount on Macs and iPads all year round to qualifying students. Read: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store.
Who qualifies? Verified students in higher education institutions – and their parents. 


When does Apple’s “Back to School” deal start?

				
					

				
			
The 2026 promotion

Apple





U.S. & Canada: From July 16 – September 24, 2026. (Gift cards)
U.K. & Europe: August 13 to October 22, 2026. (Gift cards)
India: From July 16 – September 24, 2026. (Apple is giving away AirPods and Apple Pencil in India)
Australia, New Zealand, Brazil and South Korea: January 7 to – early March 11 2026.
In North America, Apple’s annual “College Student Offer” promotion started on Thursday, July 16, and finishes on Thursday, September 24, 2026.
Because the academic summer break begins and ends later in Europe, the promotion launched slightly later in the U.K. and across Europe. There is began on August 13 and will run until October 22.
The deal ran from January 7 to early March 11 this year in the Southern Hemisphere. 
Similar timings are expected in 2027.


						

							


Who can get Apple’s “Back to School” give-away? 
Current and newly accepted higher education students – and their parents

				
					

				
			
Apple




If you are enrolled at a higher education institution (post-K12 education, such as a university or college), or are the parent of a student who is enrolled, you qualify for Apple’s year-round education pricing as well as the “Back to School” promotion while it is running.
You will need to verify your eligibility before you can access the offer. Prior to May 2026, verifying student status in some countries – including the U.S. – only required an .edu email address and the name of a higher education institution. Apple has since tightened its verification requirements.
As a result, shoppers now need to verify their student status through UNiDAYS (as was already the case in the U.K.). Students are typically required to provide their name, date of birth, and school email address, then search for their institution and wait for their student status to be confirmed.
Apple’s education pricing is not available to parents buying for school-age children, but it is available to parents who are homeschooling their children.


						

							


What is Apple’s “Back to School” deal this year?

				
					

				
			
Get free money with your purchase. 

Foundry





Gift cards worth up to $150/£120 with MacBook Pro, $100/£80 with MacBook Air, iPad Air and iPad Pro.
In India, Apple is giving away AirPods/Apple Pencil/keyboard/mouse were offered with qualifying purchases, as it did for the Australian promotion earlier in 2026.
The free AirPods usually given away with this offer have a value of $129, so the $150 or $100 voucher has an almost equivalent value to that. The gift card does at least give students the freedom to decide how they would like to spend the money.
Typical savings in the education store already include:
$200/£200 off an MacBook Pro
$100/£100 off an MacBook Air
$100/£100 off an iPad Pro
$50/£50 off an iPad Air
$80/£80 off an Apple Watch Ultra 3
$40/£40 off an Apple Watch Series 11
£10/$10 off the Apple Pencil Pro
£10/$10 off the standard Apple Pencil
So the gift card represents a total saving of $350 for the MacBook Pro, $200 off the price of a MacBook Air, and $200 off an iPad Pro, and $150 off an iPad Air. 
This isn’t the first time Apple has offered gift cards. From 2022 to 2024 in the U.S., U.K., and some other regions, Apple instead offered gift cards worth up to $150/£130, depending on the products purchased during the promotional period. 
During the Australian promotion, that ran from January 7 to March 11, 2026, Apple offered free or discounted accessories – including AirPods, AirPods Pro, Apple Pencil models, and Apple Keyboard, Mouse, or Trackpad products – with the purchase of qualifying Macs and iPads. Apple is offering that promotion in India. Some European countries may still get AirPods.
The following products were offered for free or discounted, earlier in 2026:
AirPods 4
AirPods Pro 3
Magic Mouse
Magic Trackpad
Magic Keyboard
Apple Pencil Pro
Magic Keyboard (for iPad Air/iPad Pro)
Apple also offered AirPods giveaways during its 2025 promotion, and, previously, Apple also included a discount for the AirPods Max.
Can students qualify for other savings at Apple?
Yes. Apple’s “Back to School” promotion is not the only education-related discount the company offers. Macs and iPads sold through Apple’s Education Store are discounted year-round, so qualifying students and educational institutions can save on the price of a Mac or iPad at any time of the year.
The summertime Back to School promotion is offered in addition to these ongoing education discounts. We explain everything you need to know about qualifying for Apple’s education pricing – including how much you can save and how to shop through the Apple Education Store – in our Guide to shopping in the Apple Education Store.
If you are unsure which device to buy, we also have guides to the Best Mac for Students and the Best iPad for Students.
Students can also take advantage of the discounted Apple Music Student Plan, which includes access to Apple TV+ at no extra cost. Read: How to get the student deal for Apple Music and free Apple TV+.


						

							


How to get Apple’s “Back to School” deal
In order to get Apple’s “Back to School” Deal you need to purchase a qualifying Mac or iPad from your local Apple Education Store during the promotional period. 
You will need to verify your student status via UNiDAYS, as explained above. 
Visit the Apple Education Store for your region using the links below:
U.S.
U.K.
Canada
Australia
New Zealand
Brazil
South Korea
India
France
Germany
Logging in from your university network may help simplify the verification process. 
When you purchase a qualifying Mac or iPad, you will then be able to claim the gift card.


						

							


Which products qualify for Apple’s “Back to School” deal this year? 

				
					

				
			
Apple’s Back To School deal in 2025.

Apple




The following products qualify for the the 2026 promotion in North America, the U.K. and Europe.
MacBook Air
MacBook Pro
iPad Pro 
iPad Air
Did Apple include the MacBook Neo in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Since the Australian promotion ended, Apple has launched the MacBook Neo, a new laptop aimed specifically at students.
Apple has not included the MacBook Neo in the deal for the U.S., U.K. or anywhere else.
This is no surprise. While the new MacBook is clearly targeted at students, we did not expect Apple to include it in the promotion because of its already relatively low starting price.
Did Apple include the Mac mini in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has previously allowed the purchase of a Mac mini to qualify for the promotion, but not in 2025 or in 2026.
With the launch of a new Mac mini in August 2026, which won’t ship until late September, it’s absence from the promotion is no surprise.
In recent times, the Mac mini has surged in popularity, especially among AI developers looking for a relatively inexpensive Apple Silicon machine capable of handling local AI workloads. This popularity, combined with ongoing global component shortages, has left Mac mini supply severely constrained throughout much of 2026.
Did Apple include the iPad A16 in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has previously allowed entry-level iPads to qualify for its Back to School promotion, but that was not the case in 2025 and it is not the case in 2026.
With a new entry-level iPad expected later in 2026 – and the current iPad A16 lacking support for Apple Intelligence — so our recommendation would be to choose an iPad Air instead.
Did Apple include the iPad mini in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has included the iPad mini in some Back to School promotions in the past. This year it is not included. A new iPad mini is expected to launch in 2026, so we would recommend waiting for that. 
Did Apple include the iPhone in the 2026 “Back to School” promotion?
Apple has never included the iPhone, Apple Watch, or any products other than selected Macs and iPads as qualifying purchases for its “Back to School” promotion.


						

							


How much can you save in Apple’s student deal? 

				
					

				
			
Apple




Students can already save up to $200/£220 on Macs and up to $100/£100 on iPads year-round through Apple’s Education Store. Read more here: How to get an Apple student discount at Apple’s Education Store.
The additional savings available through Apple’s “Back to School” promotion depend on both the product purchased and the promotional accessory being offered.
In previous promotions, students could save up to $199 by choosing a free Magic Keyboard, up to 179 with the AirPods Pro 4 ANC (with the MacBook Pro), up to $129 by selecting AirPods 4, or up to $129 by choosing an Apple Pencil Pro. Students who select more expensive accessories offered as part of the promotion, needed to pay the difference above the promotional discount amount. For example, in 2025, choosing AirPods Pro 3 required an additional payment of $70.
The gift cards giveaway means that the savings are slightly lower. With $150 and $100 gift cards on offer. 
Below, you can see the kinds of savings Apple has offered in previous years. 


						

							




U.S. “Back to School” giveaway details: 2026
In summer 2026, U.S. students making the following purchases qualifed for the following vouchers. The terms and conditions of the deal are here: U.S.
Apple’s education discounts are available all year round. Visit the U.S. Education Store and Canada Education Store for more information and year-round education pricing.


Additional spendGet

MacBook Pro $150 Gift voucher 
MacBook Air $100 Gift voucher 
iPad Air or iPad Pro$100 Gift voucher 

 



U.K. “Back to School” giveaway details: 2026

title: AT&T Responds to iOS 27's New iPhone Handoff Feature
content:
Apple added a new iPhone Handoff feature to iOS 27 that allows you to switch between two iPhones while using the same phone number on each device. T-Mobile and Deutsche Telekom are the first carriers to offer iPhone Handoff, and Apple said Verizon and EE will add support later this year, but AT&T is noncommittal about the feature.


A spokesperson for AT&T told CNET that the carrier sees "potential" in iPhone Handoff, but the company remains focused on "existing eSIM activation and transfer options." In other words, it sounds like AT&T has no imminent plans to support iPhone Handoff, but it also did not explicitly say that it will never offer the feature.

"While we see that there could be potential in capabilities like iPhone Handoff," the spokesperson replied, "our focus remains on delivering innovations that make life simpler and keep customers connected with confidence." They then pointed to "existing eSIM activation and transfer options across compatible devices."
In the U.S., T-Mobile is charging $5 per month for iPhone Handoff.

title: Apple developing screenless fitness tracker, report claims
content:
Macworld





Apple’s senior management are known to regard the wearables market as an important and lucrative one, and the company has already launched two successful wearable product lines: the Apple Watch, which effortlessly dominates the smartwatch market, and the company’s massively popular AirPods wireless earbuds. (There’s also the acclaimed Vision Pro VR headset, but that device is far too expensive to enter the mainstream.) Now Apple is plotting its next major push into the wearables space.
One option, according to a new report, is a type of health and fitness tracker. If that sounds similar to the Apple Watch (which found success at the very moment when Apple came to understand its value as a health and fitness accessory) there’s a key difference. This product would not have a screen, which simplifies its functionality, improves battery life, and brings down the price.
Writing for Bloomberg (subscription required), Mark Gurman claims Apple is currently developing prototypes of the device, but hasn’t yet decided whether or not to release it. “The project remains in a preliminary phase known internally as a technology investigation,” he explains.
Gurman explicitly draws a comparison to screenless products made by Whoop, which has already inspired several copycats. That company makes wearable devices to monitor health, stress, sleep and so on, along with an app which translates the data into analysis and coaching advice. The devices look like wristwatch straps, only without a screen.
The lack of a screen and overall simpler design mean that the Whoop 5.0, for example, is credited with 14-day battery life, as compared to the estimated 24 hours of the Apple Watch Series 12. It’s also cheaper than Apple Watch Series 12, which starts at $399, but you don’t actually pay for the hardware; instead you select a 12-month membership ($199, $239, or $359), which includes a band. But you’ll need to keep paying a subscription as long as you want to use it. Some other similar devices are cheaper still: the Fitbit Air is just $100 with no membership required.
With the Apple Watch line-up starting at $249 for the most basic (and now one year out of date) SE 3, there’s a clear gap in the company’s wearables portfolio for something leaner and more focused on health monitoring. We argued back in May that a screen-less ‘Apple Watch Neo’ was exactly what the company needs, so it’s heartening to hear that this may now happen.
But not soon, unfortunately. Gurman warns that, even if the technology investigation is successful and leads to a product release, this is unlikely to happen before 2028.

title: New Mac mini 2026: M6 and M5 Pro specs, prices and what’s changed
content:
Macworld






New Mac mini 2026: At a glance
What’s new: The 2026 Mac mini delivers much faster performance, especially for graphics and AI, thanks to the M6 and M5 Pro chips. It also brings faster storage and upgraded connectivity, with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 and 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard.
Release date: Announced on August 25, 2026
Price: From $899/£899
In August 2026, Apple launched a new Mac mini to replace the M4 and M4 Pro Mac mini which was introduced in October 2024. Externally the 2026 Mac mini looks just as it did following the redesign in October 2024 – it’s still a five-by-five-inch square with two front USB-C ports and the headphone jack, with three Thunderbolt ports, HDMI and Ethernet on the rear. It’s what’s inside that has changed.
The new Mac mini models offer new chips, the M6 and the M5 Pro. This is a similar scenario to a few years ago when Apple launched the M4 Mac Studio alongside the M3 Ultra Mac Studio. There is likely to be some confusion about the chip generations so we will explain the differences in more detail below.
These new chips offer a significant jump in performance, especially relating to AI. With this update it is particularly apparent that Apple is positioning the Mac mini as an AI machine. 


When is the new Mac mini available?
The new Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro models were announced on August 25, 2026 and started shipping on September 22.


						

							




How much does the new Mac mini cost?


ModelPrice
M6, 16GB, 256GB$899 / £899 
M6, 16GB, 512GB$1,199 / £1,199 
M5 Pro, 24GB, 512GB$1,699 / £1,699

 



Has the Mac mini price gone up?
In June 2026, Apple raised the starting price of the Mac mini by $200, from $599 to $799. The increase was part of a broader price hike across the entire Mac lineup, which Apple attributed to an unprecedented rise in component costs, particularly RAM.
We had hoped this meant Mac mini pricing would remain at the June level for the foreseeable future. Unfortunately, with the arrival of the new models, Apple has raised prices again—this time by a further $100/£100.
Here’s a breakdown of the key price changes for the Mac mini:

M4, 16GB, 256GB$599 / £599 $799 / £799 M6, $899 / £899 
M4, 16GB, 512GB$799 / £799 $999 / £999 M6, $1,199 / £1,199 
M4 Pro, 24GB, 512GB$1,399 / £1,399 $1,599 / £1,599 M5 Pro, $1,699 / £1,699

Mac mini M6 and M5 Pro specs
As well as the move from M4 and M4 Pro to M6 and M5 Pro, the Mac mini also gains storage that is up to twice as fast, according to Apple, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, 2.5Gb Ethernet. 
The M5 Pro model adds genlock support through its Thunderbolt 5 ports, for synchronizing a display and camera in professional video workflows.

				
					

				
			
The new M6 chip has launched in the Mac mini. 

Apple




Processor: M6 and M5 Pro chip compared
There may be some confusion over the chip generations in the new Mac mini. The mainstream model uses the newer M6 chip, while the more powerful model uses the older-generation M5 Pro. Pro chips are designed for heavier professional workloads, with more CPU and GPU cores, higher memory bandwidth, support for more unified memory, additional displays and faster Thunderbolt connectivity. So while M5 Pro remains the more capable chip overall, the M6 offers a significant step up from the M4 it replaces in the previous generation Mac mini. Macwelt has now tested the M6 Mac mini, and we have reviewed the M5 Pro Mac mini. Macwelt’s tests show that the M6 can lead in single-core CPU and Neural Engine performance, while the M5 Pro retains a clear advantage in multicore CPU and GPU performance.
M6: The Mac mini is the first Mac to ship with the M6 chip, replacing the M4 in the entry-level model. It features a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, up from 10 CPU and GPU cores in the previous generation, and supports up 170GB/s memory bandwidth if you choose 24GB or 32GB memory (the 16GB configuration offers 153GB/s bandwidth). Apple promises up to 40% faster CPU performance, twice the graphics performance and up to 4x faster AI performance than M4. It also introduces Apple’s first Dual 16-core Neural Engine, delivering up to twice the Neural Engine performance.
M5 Pro: The M5 Pro replaces the M4 Pro in the higher-end Mac mini and can be configured with up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU. Apple claims up to 4x faster LLM processing, 1.4x faster Blender ray-tracing performance and 1.5x faster Affinity image processing than M4 Pro. It supports up to 64GB of unified memory with 307GB/s memory bandwidth. Both chips feature Neural Accelerators in their GPU cores, but the M5 Pro’s additional CPU and GPU cores, greater memory capacity and higher bandwidth make it better suited to video production, 3D rendering, development and larger local AI models.
What the benchmarks show
Macwelt tested an M6 Mac mini with 24GB of memory and a 512GB SSD. In Geekbench 7, it scored 4,055 in single-core and 22,695 in multicore, compared with 3,277 and 15,693 for Macwelt’s M4 mini. In the same set of tests, the M6 scored higher than the M5 Pro in single-core performance (4,055 versus 3,720), but the M5 Pro led by a substantial margin in multicore performance (34,281 versus 22,695) and GPU compute. That makes the M6 a compelling choice for most buyers, while the M5 Pro better suits heavily threaded and GPU-intensive work. These are results from the configurations tested, not measurements of the base M6 or M5 Pro models.


						

							


Storage 
Apple claims up to twice the storage performance of the previous generation. In Macwelt’s Blackmagic Disk Speed Test, its M6 mini with a 512GB SSD reached approximately 6,700MB/s writing and 6,400MB/s reading, versus 3,000MB/s writing and 3,400MB/s reading on its M4 comparison machine. SSD speed can vary by capacity, so these figures may not apply to the base 256GB M6 mini.
There is a downside to the new storage design. As our report explains, Expand Mac mini’s teardown found that both the M6 and M5 Pro models have NAND storage soldered to the logic board, replacing the removable modules used in the M4 and M4 Pro. This means that, unlike the M4 and M4 Pro, the new models cannot accept a replacement internal SSD module. You can still add storage by connecting an external SSD through USB-C or Thunderbolt. 
The base 256GB M6 also uses a single NAND package rather than the dual arrangement reported for the 512GB model, potentially limiting storage performance. 
Other than that the storage capacities are as before – 256GB,  512GB, 1TB and 2TB for the M6 model and 512GB, 1TB, 2TB, 4TB and 8TB SSDs for the M5 Pro model. 


						

							


RAM
Both the M4 and M6 Mac mini can be configured with up to 32GB of unified memory. 
Both the M4 Pro and M5 Pro models can be configured with up to 64GB.


						

							


Connectivity: WiFi & Bluetooth

				
					

				
			
Simon Jary / Foundry




Wi-Fi: Both models now support Wi-Fi 7 which replaces the previous wireless standard Wi-Fi 6E.
Bluetooth: Both models also move to Bluetooth 6, replacing Bluetooth 5.3.
Ethernet: Previously faster Ethernet was an upgrade; the new models now have 2.5Gb Ethernet, with 10Gb Ethernet available as a configurable option.
Thunderbolt: The M6 Mac mini has three Thunderbolt 4 ports and the the M5 Pro version has three Thunderbolt 5 ports. This is the same as the previous generation.
Genlock: Apple has added Genlock support over USB-C. This is used for synchronising a display and camera (which can be an iPhone 17 Pro). It is aimed at professional video workflows
Display support: The M6 Mac mini will support up to two 6K displays plus one 5K display, while the M5 Pro supports up to three 6K displays. 
Other ports include two USB-C/USB 3 ports and a headphone jack on the front and HDMI and Ethernet remain on the rear, as previously.

Who is the Mac mini best for?
The M6 Mac mini is the best fit for most buyers who want a fast, compact desktop for everyday work, coding and mainstream creative tasks. Macwelt’s tests show a substantial performance gain over the M4, although its test machine had 24GB of memory and a 512GB SSD rather than the base configuration.
Choose the M5 Pro Mac mini if your work benefits from its stronger multicore CPU and GPU performance, Thunderbolt 5, greater memory bandwidth or support for more than 32GB of unified memory. Those advantages are most relevant to sustained professional work and larger local AI models.
Check the price of the configuration you need before ordering: the M5 Pro starts at $1,699/£1,699, and memory, storage and other upgrades add up quickly. Our reviewed $2,899 M5 Pro mini cost $100 more than an M5 Max Mac Studio configuration with a stronger GPU and more ports, although the Studio had 36GB of memory rather than the mini’s 48GB. See our Mac mini buying guide for advice on which model to choose and whether to wait.


						

							


Should you buy the 2026 Mac mini?
The M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini are on sale now, and independent test results are available for both models. For advice on which configuration to choose, whether to buy now or wait for a discount, and how they compare with older models, read our Mac mini buying guide

Especially since its radical redesign back in 2024, the tiny Mac mini has been put to countless different uses, from server farms to portable Macs. Now Chris Cheng of Shring Solutions has taken to YouTube to show off his turning it into a cyberdeck.
Using an M4 Mac mini, he's given it a 7-inch, 120Hz touchscreen plus a backlit keyboard with a trackpad. The whole device runs entirely on batteries and is claimed to give around six hours of non-stop video playback.

title: Your $1,500 iPhone 18 Pro Max doesn’t need a case, honest!
content:
Macworld





I’ve never dropped a smartphone in my life. Ever. I’ve grown so confident that these days I use my iPhone without a case and screen protector at all times, since the chances of disaster are clearly low. But that doesn’t mean my phones live a completely charmed life.
After months of daily use, even without a drop, the display tends to attract micro scratches, while some degree of battery degradation is almost inevitable. It’s all part of the natural wear and tear that serves as a reminder that even premium hardware is ultimately a consumable.
The iPhone 17 Pro launched with a ton of fundamental changes to its internal and external designs back in September 2025. We got a new set of build materials, second-generation Ceramic Shield, a larger battery, improved thermal management, and much more. These modifications have noticeably impacted the iPhone’s durability—both positively and negatively. Having used an iPhone 17 Pro Max without protection since day one, I’m ready to evaluate how this latest flagship holds up.
Even though I was using an iPhone 17 Pro for this article, the conclusions apply to the iPhone 18 Pro, which has the same aluminum body and Ceramic Shield glass. In fact, when I traded in my iPhone 17 Pro Max last week to upgrade to the new model, the salesclerk could not believe it had been used for a full year without any form of protection. After thorough inspection of the display and back, he could only spot the smallest of blemishes.
More chipping, less cracking
While Pro iPhones have always featured the iconic triple-camera layout, their build materials have shifted over the years. The iPhone 11 Pro debuted with a stainless steel frame, a standard that held for the next three models. Although this construction generally didn’t chip, it did attract obvious scuffs and fingerprint smudges. With the iPhone 15 Pro and 16 Pro, Apple switched to a titanium alloy, which made the frame tougher and less prone to scratches. Then the iPhone 17 Pro came along, retiring titanium in favor of aluminum.
Aluminum is weaker than titanium, making the latest iPhone more susceptible to dents if dropped. I haven’t dropped mine to confirm, but it’s basic science. More importantly, the frame now chips easily with regular use—something I’ve never experienced with previous Pro iPhones I’ve owned. Even though I don’t use the Camera Control button, the aluminum around it has become nicked. The sharp, raised edge of the Pro camera system area has similarly chipped, revealing the silver metal beneath the blue finish.
Other design concerns include the small gap between the metal frame and back glass panel, which actively collects dust particles. That’s not to mention that the glass panel itself leaves visible marks when I attach a MagSafe charger, requiring me to rigorously polish it to restore the shine.
Looking at the bigger picture, minimizing the use of glass has made the iPhone’s back more durable. Unlike with previous models, a drop would now chip or bend the aluminum instead of cracking the expensive glass sheet. The iPhone 17 Pro’s aesthetics may not age as gracefully, but it’s certainly a more functional phone now.

				
					

				
			The Camera Control button showed some nicks around the edge.
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The toughest screen yet 
The durability of the screen is arguably more significant than that of any other component; it’s the part you’ll be viewing and interacting with, and any imperfections to its smooth surface will be distractingly obvious. With this in mind I always place my iPhone in a separate pocket on its own, away from keys and other sharp objects. I also avoid putting it face down on solid surfaces such as restaurant tables. For years, this approach has protected my iPhone’s screen from big scratches—but there was no escaping the micro abrasions that are particularly noticeable in direct sunlight after months of regular use.
At the iPhone 17 launch event, Apple boasted about the display’s Ceramic Shield 2, which supposedly triples its scratch resistance. I initially dismissed this marketing lingo, as upgrading my iPhone annually typically makes it hard to notice these types of iterative introductions. Boy, was I wrong.
After seven months of use without a screen protector, my iPhone 17 Pro Max’s display has zero micro scratches. This is the first time in my life I’ve managed to use a smartphone this long without the screen developing any sort of surface damage. I haven’t changed the way I handle it; the Ceramic Shield 2 is just that much better at resisting scratches, maintaining the phone’s pristine look.
To avoid any chipping, nicking, scratching, and shattering, take a look at Macworld’s reviews of the best cases for iPhone 18 Pro series.

				
					

				
			Spot the scratch. You may be looking for a while.
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




Better thermals, less battery degradation
Beyond the cosmetics, the battery plays a major role when evaluating a smartphone’s durability. I typically connect my iPhone to a wired charger when its battery level drops to 20 percent and disconnect it right after it reaches 100 percent. I occasionally rely on a MagSafe charger and leave it plugged in overnight without enabling any optimized battery charging features. Within 6 months, the battery’s maximum capacity would usually drop to 95 percent or so.
With the iPhone 17 Pro, Apple introduced an aluminum build and vapor chamber for improved thermal management, along with a larger battery. (The 18 Pro brings a a next-generation vapor chamber with a new design built for improves sustained performance.) These changes minimize overheating and stretch the flagship’s battery life remarkably, slowing down the degradation cycle. While I still follow the same charging and usage routines, my iPhone 17 Pro Max’s maximum battery capacity stayed near 100 percent longer than ever, and the 18 Pro should do event better. So users holding on to their iPhones for multiple years won’t need to have the batteries replaced as often.

				
					

				
			Battery health degrades more slowly than in the past.
Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




Conclusions: Amazingly durable, with room for improvement
This wasn’t the perfect performance across the board, and Apple has left room for improvement in future generations. This isn’t unusual: radically transformed products are often riddled with imperfections that manufacturers address in the years that follow. The MacBook Air M3, for example, added an anodization seal to minimize fingerprints on the Midnight variant following M2 user complaints. Apple could similarly tweak the iPhone’s aluminum coating to limit chipping. The back glass panel on the iPhone 18 Pro is now color-matched to the body, but it has the same Ceramic Shield scratch resistance rather than the 2nd-gen process used on the front glass.
As for the display’s resistance, I’m genuinely impressed by how the Ceramic Shield 2 is holding up: 10 out of 10, no notes. The battery life and thermal management have likewise become more reliable than ever. At this point, any groundbreaking changes to the battery will probably require dropping the lithium-ion technology in favor of something completely different. Once a fragile glass sandwich, the iPhone Pro has become a beacon of durability and dependability.

title: New iPhone Setting Lets Users Shake Off Motion-Sensing Ads
content:
Apple is testing an iPhone setting for users in China that lets them add apps to a list that prevents them from accessing the device's motion sensors. Apple hasn't explicitly said what the setting is in response to, but Chinese apps sometimes show "shake-to-open" ads on launch, and they can be triggered by merely picking up an iPhone, walking, or going over a bump in a car, resulting in unwanted redirects.

title: Feds support Apple's arguments ahead of Epic Supreme Court judgement
content:
While the US DOJ won't take sides in a case, the Solicitor General did file a brief that the ruling that Apple violated "the spirit of the injunction" wasn't within legal standards.


Apple is ready to face the Supreme Court in October
The Apple vs Epic lawsuit has been ongoing for over six years. It started as an intentional violation of Apple's App Store rules, which led to the lawsuit and almost total victory for Apple on all but one charge.
Apple was ordered to remove its anti-steering practices, which it did, but was found in violation of the injunction due to not following the spirit of the injunction. After more than a year of back and forth, the Supreme Court will soon weigh in on the matter, and various firms have filed amicus briefs ahead of the October decision.

title: Best Mac 2026: Every Apple Mac and MacBook compared
content:
Macworld






Which Mac is best for you? 
Whether you want everyday portability, professional creative power, desktop performance, or budget-friendly computing, Apple’s lineup has a Mac that fits. For $699 you can own a MacBook Neo, which is Apple’s most affordable laptop. Spend a little more and the MacBook Air excels at everyday work and battery life, while the MacBook Pro lineup delivers the extra power required by demanding professional workloads. If you prefer a desktop, the iMac is a great all-in-one option for the home, while Mac mini offers good value if you don’t need portability and already have a display and accessories. At the top end, the Mac Studio is built for intensive professional workloads, including demanding creative work and AI development.
Choosing the best Mac in 2026 isn’t simply about buying the newest model; it’s about finding the Mac that best matches what you need from a computer. Apple’s lineup ranges from ultraportable MacBooks to powerful desktop Macs, with options for students, everyday users, creatives and professionals.
In this Mac buying guide, we cover everything you need to know about the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, Mac mini, iMac and Mac Studio, including the differences in size, specs, features and price. We’ll help you decide which Mac and configuration offers the right balance of value, performance and portability for you.
Best Mac 2026: Mac & MacBook Buyers Guide
Our top Mac for most people in 2026 is the MacBook Air. It offers an excellent combination of performance, portability and value in a compact package that will suit the typical Mac user.
If you need more power, we recommend the MacBook Pro, which delivers high-end performance in a portable form. At the other end of the price range, the new MacBook Neo starts at $699/£699 and is Apple’s most affordable Mac laptop.
If you don’t need a laptop, Apple also has some excellent desktop options. The Mac Studio offers exceptional performance for the money and can save thousands compared with a similarly specified Mac laptop, while the Mac mini is Apple’s cheapest desktop Mac, starting at $899/£899.
Below, we take you through every Mac currently available from Apple, explaining who each model is best suited to and what you should consider when choosing a configuration. You’ll also find live prices to help you find the best deal today. For more help choosing between Apple’s laptops, see our MacBook comparison.
Price increases June 2026
In June 2026, Apple increased prices significantly across several product lines including Macs, iPads, the Apple TV 4K, and HomePod models, citing an unprecedented rise in component costs. 
The company stated it had “never seen a component price increase this much, this quickly” and that it had shielded customers from these increases for as long as possible before finally raising prices. 
For Macs, prices increased from $100/£100 to $500/£500 depending on the model.

What is it? The 13-inch MacBook Air is Apple’s thin and light laptop for everyday use, offering more performance and features than the cheaper MacBook Neo.
What’s new? Apple introduced the M5 MacBook Air in March 2026, featuring the M5 chip with its faster CPU and GPU. The base configuration now starts with 512GB of storage (double the previous model), along with faster SSD speeds, more memory bandwidth, and support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
Who’s it for? It’s perfect for students and everyday users who want a lightweight laptop that’s easy to carry, and powerful enough for working, studying, browsing, and doing light creative work. If you want a larger screen there is a 15-inch MacBook Air, which we discuss below. 
How much does the 13-inch MacBook Air cost? The entry-level 13-inch M5 MacBook Air costs from $1,299/£1,299, that’s up $200/£200 from the launch price of $1,099/£1,099. You can create build-to-order models with more memory (up to 32GB) or storage (up to 4TB).

What are display specifications?

The 13.6-inch Liquid Retina on the M5 MacBook Air display has a native resolution of 2,560×1,664 and 500 nits brightness.
The MacBook Air M5 can support two external displays.
How do I connect stuff? The M5 MacBook Air models supports Thunderbolt 4, which means that they can support a dual monitor set up. If you want to connect USB-A devices, you need either a USB-C to USB-A adapter, like Apple’s $19 / £19 one, or a USB-C hub that has USB-A ports. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately. See our round-up of the best USB-C hubs and adapters.
The 2026 MacBook Air offers Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) for connecting to a network. It also provides built-in Bluetooth (6) for wirelessly connecting a mouse or other peripherals. If you want to connect to an ethernet network, you need an adapter.
How fast is it? In our tests the M5 saw consistent gains over the M4 in the previous generation, as you can see in our Mac processor benchmarks. In some benchmarks the M5 even beats the M1 Ultra. If you are upgrading from an old Mac – especially if it is one with an Intel chip – you will see a huge difference.
Any other considerations? The MacBook Air should be more than fast enough for general-purpose use. The only issue is that, because it doesn’t have an internal fan, it may slow down during long processing sessions to keep cool. So if you are likely to be video editing or compiling code the MacBook Pro with its fan is a better choice. Also note that it’s impossible to upgrade the storage or memory after purchase, so you should buy the model with the largest amount of storage and memory you can afford or invest in external storage. 
Why we recommend the 13-inch MacBook Air: The MacBook Air is a great choice for someone who does general-purpose work and moves around a lot, such as a student or a self-employed person.

Who’s it for? The MacBook Neo is designed to appeal to students and those who want to use a laptop for everyday tasks like web browsing, video calls, schoolwork, streaming, email and office apps. Because it uses an A18 Pro iPhone chip and is limited to 8GB of non-upgradable RAM, it is not suitable for heavy video editing or large-scale photo processing.
How much does the MacBook Neo cost? At launch the MacBook Neo was the cheapest Mac laptop Apple has ever released, starting at $599/£599. That price is now slightly more, at $699/£699, but it’s still about half the price of a MacBook Air.

How fast is it? MacBook Neo uses the A18 Pro chip that first appeared in the iPhone 16 Pro. Our tests and benchmarks of that chip indicate that it offers similar performance to the M1. It is suitable for everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming, and office apps.
Any other considerations? To get to the low price Apple has made several trade-offs. The MacBook Neo lacks Thunderbolt and MagSafe support, there is no keyboard backlight and no Touch ID on the base model, and RAM is limited to 8GB with no option to increase that to 16GB.
Why we recommend the MacBook Neo: This is the most affordable way to own a Mac laptop – unless you buy a used or refurbished model. If you don’t need pro-level performance it’s a very compelling entry-point into Apple’s ecosystem.

Any other considerations? The Air doesn’t have a fan to keep the computer cool, so it may throttle down its speed during long processing sessions, such as video editing or compiling code. What is it? There are three distinct types of MacBook Pro, the M5 model discussed here, and the M5 Pro and M5 Max models we look at separately. Like its more powerful siblings, the M5 MacBook Pro has an HDR ProMotion display, which the MacBook Air lacks. The MacBook Pro offers more ports than the MacBook Air: HDMI and SDXC slots. The 14-inch MacBook Pro offers 24 hour battery life – which, along with the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro chip, is the best battery life ever on a MacBook.
What’s new? In October 2025 Apple updated the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 chip. There were no other major changes, aside from the new option to add 4TB storage at point of sale. Bigger changes came with the launch of the M4 MacBook Pro in October 2024, back then we saw RAM increase from 8GB to 16GB as standard, camera improvements, and Thunderbolt 4 support.
Who’s it for? The 14-inch MacBook Pro is for a more demanding user than the MacBook Air. Its main benefit is the design allows for better cooling, which means that if you push the machine it won’t slow down to avoid overheating. However, there are other MacBook Pros available from Apple (including a 16-inch model) that offer faster processors, so if you really need a powerful machine one of those might be more suitable–we discuss the M5 Pro and M5 Max models below. 
How much does the 14-inch MacBook Pro cost? The entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 starts at $1,999/£1,999 (up from the $1,699/£1,699 it cost in March 2026 – even that was an increase compared to the $1,599/£1,599 it cost at launch in October 2025).
What are the specifications? The standard specs for the 14-inch MacBook Pro offer an improvement on the previous generation. The MacBook Pro now ships with 1TB SSD as standard, up from 512GB. 
Apple M5, 10-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16GB memory, 1TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 4 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $1,999/£1,999.

What are display specifications?

The notch at the top of the display conceals the 12MP FaceTime camera which now features Centre Stage.
How do I connect stuff? There are three Thunderbolt 4 ports. These are compatible with USB-C (if you have wired devices that aren’t USB-C, you’ll need an adapter, we have a separate MacBook Pro Thunderbolt adapter guide to help you decide which ones you’ll need). The 14-inch MacBook Pro also comes with an HDMI port for connecting an external display or projector, and an SDXC Card slot for plugging in memory cards from cameras, audio recorders, and other devices. The HDMI port also supports multichannel audio output. The 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro still has the older Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax) and Bluetooth 5.3 for wireless connectivity (the other MacBook Pro models and Air have been updated to the newer standards. In the U.K. and Europe Apple has stopped including a Power Adapter in the box, so you will need to buy one separately.
How fast is it? Apple described the M5 chip in the MacBook Pro as offering a “big leap” in AI performance thanks to a Neural Accelerator in each core. It also offers 4x better graphics performance compared to the M4, according to Apple. In some of our tests the M5 beat the M1 Ultra, which shows the progress Apple has made with its silicon over the past few years. The MacBook Air matches the specs of the M5 MacBook Pro, but the Pro outperforms the Air due to the inclusion of a fan for cooling (the MacBook Air doesn’t have the space for this). If you need it, more power is available from the MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or Max.
Any other considerations? Our advice is to max out the RAM (aka Unified Memory) and storage when you buy a Mac because you can’t update it later on.
Why we recommend the 14-inch MacBook Pro (M5): The 14-inch MacBook Pro costs $1,999/£1,999, which is much more than the 13-inch MacBook Air at $1,299/£1,299. However the $700/£700 difference is misleading: when comparing like for like: the 15-inch MacBook Air with 1TB SSD costs $1,799/£1,799, which is $200/£200 less than the 14-inch MacBook Pro with the same 1TB SSD. There’s a larger 16-inch MacBook Pro with similar specs that we discuss below. 
What’s new? The 14-inch MacBook Pro with M5 Pro or M5 Max was introduced in March 2026 and introduces Apple’s new Fusion Architecture chip that combines two 3nm CPU and GPU dies into a single unified system on a chip, which lets Apple scale performance and efficiency. In addition, the GPU includes a Neural Accelerator in every core, which Apple claims delivers up to 4x the AI performance of the previous generation. There is also faster memory and faster SSD speeds.
Who’s it for? If your work demands serious processing power, these machines are built to handle it. If you regularly work in professional software, the 14-inch MacBook Pro is a strong choice, and with either the M5 Pro or M5 Max chip they’re the most powerful laptops Apple has ever made. The 14-inch model costs less than the 16-inch version, making it the more budget-friendly option, and if you use an external monitor the screen size matters less. The M5 Pro MacBook Pro is designed for demanding professional tasks like software development, managing large photo libraries, or editing 4K video, while the M5 Max is aimed at even heavier workflows such as 3D animation, complex simulations, AI development, and high-end video production.
How much does the 14-inch MacBook Pro, M5 Pro & Max cost? The price now starts at $2,499/£2,499 (up from $2,199/£2,199) for the M5 Pro. The M5 Max version starts at $4,099/£4,099, up from $3,599/£3,599 prior to June 2026, and a gigantic leap from the previous generation starting price of $3,199/£3,199 (that M4 Max model came with 1TB SSD rather than 2TB).
What are the specifications? Here are the standard configurations for the 14-inch MacBook Pro. 
Apple M5 Pro, 15-core CPU, 16-core GPU, 24GB memory, 1TB SSD, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, SDXC, HDMI, $2,499/£2,499.

What are display specifications?

You’ll also get a 1,000,000-to-1 contrast ratio and ProMotion support with a refresh rate up to 120Hz.

What are the display specifications? The 24-inch 4.5K Retina display has 11.3 million pixels and supports the P3 wide color gamut, over a billion colors, 500 nits of brightness, and True Tone. Apple treats the display with an anti-reflective coating to help with readability. The display hasn’t changed since the M1 model launched.
How do I connect stuff? The $1,499 24-inch iMac has two Thunderbolt 4 ports that also work with USB-C devices. The $1,699 and $1,899 iMacs have four Thunderbolt 4 ports (the previous generation had two Thunderbolt/USB 4 and two USB 3 ports). If you have a USB-A device, you need to buy an adapter, such as Apple’s ($19 / £19). If you have multiple USB-A devices and other items, consider a Thunderbolt hub. The 24-inch iMac also has a headphone jack on the side.
Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 are built-in. Apple doesn’t put a gigabit ethernet port on the 24-inch iMac—instead, it’s on the power adapter. But that ethernet-equipped power adapter comes standard with the $1,699 and $1,899 models. It’s not included with the $1,499 model, but you can select it as an option at the point of purchase—and yes, that means you’ll have to pay extra for it.
How fast is it?: The 24-inch iMac is the only Mac still using the M4 chip, so it’s not as fast as the other Macs, but it’s still got all the speed general consumers need, and it can even handle pro applications with no problem. However, the $1,499 model has only one fan inside its body, while the $1,699 and $1,899 models have two fans. That means the high-priced models do a better job of keeping the internals cool. The $1,499 model may need to slow down its performance on heavy-duty tasks in order to maintain a proper temperature.
Any other considerations? The iMac doesn’t represent particularly good value at its current price. A better buy is the MacBook Air, which offers a faster M5 chip with a 10-core CPU, 8-core GPU, 16GB of memory, and a 512GB SSD for $1,299/£1,299. By comparison, the iMac costs $1,499/£1,499 yet includes an older M4 chip with an 8-core CPU, 8-core GPU, the same 16GB of memory, and only a 256GB SSD. We feel that the iMac price is high compared to the specs on offer, but we do admire the design. We are holding out for a bigger screen. Apple is rumored to launch an M6 iMac in 2027.
Why we recommend the iMac (M4): The iMac was transformed when Apple introduced the redesigned 24-inch model in 2021, with major improvements to its design, display, and performance. If you’re buying one today, the $1,699/£1,699 model is the sweet spot, adding more ports, Touch ID, and Ethernet. We’d still love to see Apple revive the iMac Pro with a larger display, and sincerely hope one is in the pipeline. 

							
		
Which Mac is best for what you do?
In the table below you can find the best Mac for every use case we can think of. Find the Mac that is best for you and meets your needs below. 


WhoRecommended MacWhy

Most people13-inch MacBook Air (M5)The best balance of performance, portability, battery life and price for everyday work.
Small budgetMacBook NeoApple’s cheapest laptop and plenty powerful enough for web browsing, email, streaming and basic productivity.
StudentsMacBook NeoAffordable, portable and capable enough for schoolwork, research, video calls and everyday apps.
Commuters13-inch MacBook Air (M5)Thin and light with strong performance and long battery life.
Big screen/everyday use15-inch MacBook Air (M5)A larger display without the weight or expense of a 16-inch MacBook Pro.
Big screen/pro use16-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)Largest laptop display combined with outstanding battery life and workstation-class performance
Home worker15-inch MacBook Air (M5)Plenty of screen space, excellent battery life and enough performance for office and productivity work.
Family computer24-inch iMacSimple all-in-one setup that’s well suited to a shared home computer.
Receptionist24-inch iMacCompact, tidy all-in-one design with very little setup required.
Value seekerMac mini (M6)Strong everyday and creative performance in Apple’s smallest desktop.
Developer (desktop)Mac mini (M5 Pro)More CPU and GPU power than the standard mini, with active cooling for sustained workloads.
Developer (laptop)14-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)Multicore performance, ample memory options and portability.
Photographers and designers14-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro)Excellent XDR display combined with CPU and GPU performance for creative applications.
Video editor (laptop)14-inch MacBook Pro (M5 Pro or M5 Max)Powerful media engines and sustained performance while remaining reasonably portable.
Video editor (desktop)Mac Studio (M5 Max)Powerful GPU and media capabilities make it ideal for demanding 4K/8K production workflows.
Creative professionals (desktop)Mac Studio (M5 Max)Workstation-class CPU and GPU performance for video, audio, photography, development and 3D work
Music productionMac Studio (M5 Max)Quiet operation, sustained CPU performance, lots of memory and extensive connectivity.
3D rendering Mac Studio (M5 Max or M5 Ultra)The most GPU performance and memory capacity.
Large AI modelsMac Studio (M5 Ultra)Up to 512GB of unified memory plus Apple’s highest-end CPU and GPU options.

 




 FAQ 


1.
What’s best, MacBook Air or MacBook Pro?
We address this question in detail in our comparison of the MacBook Air vs Pro. It’s really a question of price versus power. The Air is sufficient for most people’s needs, the Pro will give you that extra boost in terms of what the Mac is capable of.
Buying an entry-level MacBook Air for $1,299/£1,299 will get you an excellent Mac laptop. If you want to spend less than that you may be able to find a discounted MacBook Air – we round up the best MacBook Air deals regularly.
If you want a larger screen, the 15-inch MacBook Air is a great option that is a lot cheaper than the smaller 14-inch MacBook Pro. 
The price of the Pro and Max MacBook Pro models is high, but these models offer the kind of specs professional users, especially creatives, need, including support for more RAM, and more CPU and GPU cores. If you can afford to stretch to the Max you will get the ultimate Mac without a doubt, but you need to be willing to make a significant investment.
The choice between the 14-inch and 16-inch MacBook Pro is all down to the screen size. The 16-inch models are more expensive, but once you spec them out in such a way to be comparable the price difference is minor. The bigger difference is between the Pro and Max processors. Other than speed, MacBooks with Max processors can connect up to four external displays (three over Thunderbolt and one over HDMI), while since the M4 all models allow two external displays in addition to the laptop screen. (There are workarounds if you need to connect more screens).
There is now another Mac laptop to consider, the MacBook Neo lowers the price of ownership of a Mac laptop to $699/£699. If budget really is tight though, you might want to consider a discounted previous generation MacBook Air instead.





2.
Should I upgrade from my Intel Mac?
Yes. It’s time! We are now more than six years into Apple’s transition from Intel processors to its own silicon that includes CPU, GPU, and unified memory. The transition began with the introduction of the M1 in November 2020. Since June 2023 every Mac Apple sells uses Apple’s own chips rather than Intel processors.
If you’ve yet to upgrade your Intel Mac to one powered by Apple’s silicon what are you waiting for? If you are concerned that a must-have app doesn’t run on an M-series Mac, consider finding a new app because the performance gains are tremendous.
Another good reason to replace an Intel Mac is that Apple’s support for these models is winding down. macOS Golden Gate, released in September 2026, is the first major version of macOS to support no Intel Macs. Intel Macs compatible with older versions of macOS may continue receiving security updates for a limited period, but they are now outside Apple’s current feature-release cycle. Apple does not guarantee how long those updates will continue, and machines limited to macOS Sequoia are likely to lose support sooner than those capable of running macOS Tahoe. Read: How long does Apple support Macs.





3.
Where can I get the best price for a new Mac?
Apple rarely offers direct price cuts on new hardware, but resellers frequently do. Getting the best price on a new Mac requires knowing where to look and when to buy: 
Top U.S. Retailers:
Amazon: Often has the lowest prices, especially during events like Prime Day. For example, during the July 2026 Prime Day event, a 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro was available for $1,749, a $450 discount. Even outside of events, Amazon frequently undercuts Apple’s MSRP.
Best Buy: A reliable source for discounts and trade-in offers. In late 2025, Best Buy offered a massive $1,150 off an M2 Ultra Mac Studio.
B&H Photo: A well-regarded authorized reseller that often has competitive pricing on Macs.
Walmart: Known for exclusive deals on older models, like the M1 MacBook Air, which has been sold brand-new for just $599.
Top U.K. Retailers:
Amazon UK: Similar to the U.S., Amazon UK is a primary source for discounts.
KRCS: An Apple Premium Reseller that frequently offers good deals.
John Lewis & Currys: Reliable high-street retailers that often have competitive prices and good customer service.
If you’re looking for a great offer, visit our MacBook Pro deals, MacBook Air deals, iMac deals, Mac Studio deals, and Mac mini deals pages which are regularly updated.





4.
What specs do I really need for my Mac?
Chip: The specs you need depend on what you plan to do with your Mac. For everyday tasks such as web browsing, email, office apps and light photo editing, a standard M-series chip is more than sufficient. Apple’s latest entry-level desktop chip is the M6, available in the Mac mini, while other Macs still use M4 or M5-generation chips. 
If you regularly work with complex spreadsheets, large Photoshop files, audio projects, video editing or more demanding games, look at a Pro chip. The M5 Pro Mac mini, for example, offers up to an 18-core CPU and 20-core GPU and up to 64GB unified memory.
For professional video production, 3D work, software development and other intensive workloads, a Max chip is more appropriate. The Mac Studio with M5 Max offers an 18-core CPU, up to a 40-core GPU and as much as 128GB unified memory. 
The M5 Ultra, with up to a 36-core CPU, 80-core GPU and 512GB unified memory, is aimed at the most extreme workloads, including VFX, scientific computing and running very large AI models locally.
GPU: One of the biggest differences between Apple’s chips is GPU performance. Standard M-series chips are easily sufficient for everyday graphics, casual gaming and light creative work. Pro chips add considerably more GPU power for video editing, graphics work, 3D applications and gaming. Max chips are designed for professional graphics, high-resolution video and demanding 3D workflows, while Ultra provides Apple’s highest GPU performance. The M5 Max offers up to 40 GPU cores, while the M5 Ultra doubles that to 80 GPU cores. Both also have Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core to speed up AI workloads.
RAM: Apple calls RAM Unified Memory. The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB, which is probably the biggest drawback of that machine. Most Macs start with at least 16GB, which is plenty for everyday use, although we recommend choosing more if your budget allows because the memory cannot be upgraded later. 24GB or 32GB is a good choice for heavier multitasking, photo editing, podcasting, moderate video production and gaming. Developers and professional creative users may benefit from 48GB, 64GB or more. The new M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 64GB, M5 Max Mac Studio with up to 128GB, and M5 Ultra Mac Studio with an enormous 512GB.
Storage: Even with iCloud and external drives available, it can seem like you can never have enough storage inside your Mac. 256GB may be sufficient for basic web and office use, but it can fill up quickly. We recommend 512GB for most people who want to keep a Mac for several years, particularly if you store photos, games or media locally. For regular video or audio production, 1TB or more is preferable. Professional users may need several terabytes: the M5 Pro Mac mini can be configured with up to 8TB, while Mac Studio configurations go even higher. As with unified memory, internal Mac storage cannot be upgraded after purchase, so it is worth thinking about future requirements when ordering.
For more information to help you decide which Mac to buy see our Mac processor comparison where we compare Apple silicon and Intel. We also offer advice about how much storage, RAM, and cores in How much MacBook RAM, SSD, GPU, and CPU do you really need.





5.
When were the Macs last updated?
In August 2026 the Mac mini and Mac Studio were updated. 
In March 2026 the MacBook Pro and MacBook Air were updated, and the MacBook Neo was introduced.
The most recent iMac update was in October 2024.
The Mac Pro has been discontinued. 





Why you can trust Macworld’s advice
Macworld has been covering everything Apple related since our first issue which arrived alongside the original Mac in 1984. Nobody knows Apple better, except probably Apple, but the difference is that we are completely impartial. We are made up of a team of experts with decades of experiences with Macs and other Apple products, and between us we have reviewed every Apple product meaning we are uniquely positioned to provide buying advice.
